properties.Description: Description: The amount of the invoice. Enterable: PO Costing: If the invoice will be costed against a PO it should include all adonns applicable to this invoice. Credit Memos: If you are entering a Credit Memo the amount of the invoice cannot be greater than the amount of the remaining amount of the invoice. Reversal: If you are entering a Reversal you will not be able to enter an amount. The system will default the entire amount of the invoice you are reversing. Foreign Vendor: If you are using a foreign vendor the amount should be entered in foreign currency. Canadian Taxes: If your SASC country flag is 'ca' a window will appear for entry of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) amount and Provincial Services Tax (PST). These amounts will be deducted from the invoice amount and posted to the account codes set up for this Vendor in APSV. Allowable values: This field can up to 12 integers including 2 decimal positions. The field must be greater than zero. Content:

properties.Description: This is the invoice number for the transaction you are processing. Duplicate active invoices are allowed. Once the invoice becomes inactive you will be allowed to re-use it. An existing invoice number is required when entering a credit memo, debit memo or reversal. An invoice number is not required for a rebate. Allowable values: Up to 15 character positions can be entered into this field. Dashes, slashes, periods, letters, numbers etc.. are all acceptable characters that can be entered into this field. Release dependent information: As of 5.0/5.1 transaction types of Miscellaneous Credits and Credit Memos require invoice numbers and the amounts are stored as negative values. When going live to 5.0/5.1 the conversion program sequentially assigned all type 5 and 6 records an invoice number.

Transactions which are disputed will only be affected when you attempt to perform Accounts Payable Pay Invoices Due (APEP). You will not be allowed to pay disputed invoices. Disputed transactions will print on the APRC report under the disputed column. This will allow you to review them before processing APEP. Enterable: Invoices (transcd = 0), Misc. Credits (transcd = 5), and Debit Memos (transcd = 8) are the only transactins which may be disputed. properties.Label: Immed Pay
properties.Help: Immediate Pay - If 'Yes', Inoivce Will be Paid on a Cash Basis
properties.Description: Immediate Payment option is only available with invoice transactions. Immediate Payment indicates you will pay the Vendor immediately for the amount of the invoice instead of updating the Vendor current balance. The Invoice (transcd = 0), Manual Payment(transcd =7), and Scheduled Payment (transcd = 3) transactions automatically become inactive. Enterable: The Immediate Payment option is only available with invoice transactions (transcd = 0). This option is not supported for foreign currency transactions. The Vendor's General Ledger bank and discount accounts will automatically be updated instead of the Vendor's General Ledger addon and expense/asset accounts. You are expected to print a check for the amount of the invoice immediately after completing the transaction. This can be done by processing Accounts Payable Check Print (APEC). By entering in the value of "y" the system will display "yes" into this field. If "n" is entered into this field the system will display "no".

properties.Label: Geo Code
properties.Description: Taxware Sales and Use Tax (SUT) uses the geo code to determine which taxes should be applied if there is more than one taxing jurisdiction within a zip code. Examples of this are when a zip code crosses county lines and each county has a different tax rate or when multiple cities exist in the same zip code and each city has a different tax rate. Each taxing jurisdiction within the zip code is given a unique, two-digit identifier. Taxware uses the city name, state, zip code and geo code to find the correct tax rates. Taxware Enterprise (TWE) uses the geo code as a unique identifier of a taxing jurisdiction and not a supplemental identifier as in SUT. With TWE, all jusrisdictions world-wide have a geo code. Each geo code can include country, state or province, county, city and district taxing jurisdictions. Any taxing jurisdiction except country can be omitted from the definition of a geo code. TWE can apply the correct tax rates based on the geo code alone. Content:

properties.Label: Allow Generic Prod Rebate
properties.Description: Added with JIRA SXWEB-38291/SXWEB-39527. This field sets this vendor to participate on the Generic Rebates logic for Vendor on Sale rebates, when checked. It is located in APSV – Ordering – Rebates section with the label “Use Generic Rebates”. When a product is entered on the OE line, the vendor is looked up – in ICSW, ICSC, or from OEEL depending on the product being a stock, catalog, or non-stock product – to determine if that vendor is a generic product rebate vendor based on the APSV allow generic rebates flag. If that vendor allows generic rebates, the PDSR rebate logic will ignore the assigned vendor, except to limit the choices to vendors who use generic rebates. As soon as a record is found, ignoring the vendor, that rebate will be used and then the logic will continue to use all other criteria for finding the best rebate to use, e.g., it will still use the Customer Rebate Types listed for the customer in ARSC/ARSS and any other criteria such as customer/shipto/warehouse. So it is just ignoring the vendor when searching for the rebate to use but does not ignore any other criteria. Usage of this logic requires AOData PD - PDGenericVendProdRebateFl to be checked. This can be found in AO – Products – Rebates – Rebates Options section with the label “Allow Generic Product Rebates”. Content:

properties.Description: Used on acknowledgements that are VMI specific orders. Database default is 'no', so will still create orders as Quote orders until set to yes. Used in the 855in Purchase Order Acknowledgement interface (EDEPA) for ION or EDI. It is used as a replacement of adding an option to the report for EDI processing of EDEPA 855in. If turned on, the BOD Interface will create Purchase Orders as PO orders, not QU orders. Allows the distributor to skip the process of validating all the purchase order data first and then convert the Quote orders to PO orders for processing. If the vendor is a trusted vendor and sends reliable updates and changes to the purchase orders, then use this option. The logic changed is also used in POEVP where outbound edi852 PO orders are created. Option to create empty PO orders for the Vendor to use based on the recommndeded inventory to reorder. properties.Label: Geo Code
properties.Description: Taxware Sales and Use Tax (SUT) uses the geo code to determine which taxes should be applied if there is more than one taxing jurisdiction within a zip code. Examples of this are when a zip code crosses county lines and each county has a different tax rate or when multiple cities exist in the same zip code and each city has a different tax rate. Each taxing jurisdiction within the zip code is given a unique, two-digit identifier. Taxware uses the city name, state, zip code and geo code to find the correct tax rates. Taxware Enterprise (TWE) uses the geo code as a unique identifier of a taxing jurisdiction and not a supplemental identifier as in SUT. With TWE, all jusrisdictions world-wide have a geo code. Each geo code can include country, state or province, county, city and district taxing jurisdictions. Any taxing jurisdiction except country can be omitted from the definition of a geo code. TWE can apply the correct tax rates based on the geo code alone. Content:

properties.Label: Addon
properties.Description: This array field has 2 occurances: Addon 1 Addon 2 These addons will default in from the ARSCO record. The addonamt is also updated from order entry during invoice processing. See addonamt field in oeeh for a further description. Content:

properties.Label: Amount
properties.Description: This is the dollar amount for this transaction. This is enterable by the user in ARET. This is also updated during invoice processing. The total invoice amount on the order will become the amount on the ARET record.

properties.Label: Applied Inv Dt
properties.Description: This field is updated on schedule pay (type 11), credit memo (type 6), and debit memo (type 8) records in the following mannor: Type 11 - schedule pay: This is the date that a credit memo or debit memo is applied to this schedule pay. The date comes in from the invoice date entered in aret for the credit memo or debit memo. Or, the invoice date of the RM applied through invoice processing. Type 06,08 - credit memo/debit memo: This is the date of the invoice this has been applied to. Misc credit or unapplied cash amounts applied in arece do NOT update this field.

properties.Label: Applied Inv #
properties.Description: This field is updated on the following records: 11- schedule pay 06 - credit memo 08 - debit memo On the type 11, this is the invoice number of the credit memo, misc credit, or debit memo. On the type 06 and 08 this is the invoice number this transaction was applied to.

properties.Label: Applied Inv Suffix
properties.Description: The applied invoice suffix. The suffix will be 00 - 98 if the invoice was created through invoice processing. The suffix will be -99 for invoices created in ARET.

properties.Label: Tran Type
properties.Description: This is the code of the transaction that was applied to this particular invoice. example: 05 - misc credit 06 - credit memo 08 - debit memo On the credit memo, misc credit or debit memo invoice, the apptranscd would be the transaction code of the invoice it was applied against. example: 00 - invoice 01 - service charge 04 - cod

properties.Label: Check #
properties.Description: The check number applied to this invoice/schedule pay. This field can be updated the following ways: The check is posted through ARECE. The check number is stored on the invoice (type 0) and the scheduled pay (type 11) record. The invoice record stores the most recently applied check number. The check is received through Order Entry Received On Account. The check number is stored on the Unappplied Cash (type 3) record. The check is posted through Order Entry downpayment. The check number is stored on the manual payment record (type 7). Miscellaneous credits (type 5) applied in arece with a cash posting transaction, the check number will be stored on the misc credit record.

properties.Label: Check#
properties.Description: This field is updated on type 3 (unapplied cash) records. The field is updated with the check number being applied in arece when the unapplied cash is being applied. Only updated when the unapplied cash is inactivated. This field is not enterable by the user.

properties.Label: COD Collected
properties.Description: The purpose of this field is to collect an additional amount from the customer to go towards a past due amount. The amount will then display in arece when paying the cod. The amount does NOT display in arit. Amount is calculated in pmep, if the customer has an arsa record. Will also be calculated if invoice is cod, and additional amount entered in oees, or oeir. Amount is updated from the oeeh.codcollamt field. updated in oeepia.p and p-oeepip.i. Read in arececod.p and p-arra.i.

properties.Label: Company #
properties.Description: Identifies the Company under which the record was created.

properties.Label: Cash Rec Applied Jrnl #
properties.Description: This is the arece journal number. This field is updated when type 5 (misc credit) and type 3(unapplied cash) transactions are applied in arece. Program that updates this field is areceu1.p Field is displayed in arit for inactive type 3 and 5 transactions. Not enterable by user.

This is the set number of the arece posting journal. Only updates type 5 (misc credit) and type 3 (unapplied cash) transactions. This set number is not displayed in arit. Updated in areceu1.p and displays on ar journal print. Not enterable by the user.

properties.Label: Customer #
properties.Description: The customer number for this invoice. This field is entered in arece, aret and oeet.

properties.Label: Discount
properties.Description: The amount of discount actually taken, versus the original discount amount calculated for this invoice. This field is updated when the schedule pay is paid. Initially defaults in as zero. updated on the type 00, 11, 07, and 05 records.

This is the date the invoice must be paid otherwise the order discount is considered lost. This date is calculated from the disount days on the terms record set up in sastt. Each customer will have a terms type set up on the arsc required screen. This date can be overrode in aret, aremo and aremp.

This field has a value of y/n. This field designates a transaction as disputed. Transactions that are disputed are not aged or service charged. This field is enterable by the user in aret and aremo. Transactions that are disputed display a 'h' next to the invoice date of the schedule pay in arit and a 'd' next to the seq number of the schedule pay in arece. There is a dispute field on the f6 detail record in aret. This will display yes on the schedule pay records. If the invoice was not entered as disputed, but was flagged as disputed in aremo, the invoice detail will show 'no' in the dispute field. However, the PY will show yes. This is because the invoice was not disputed at time of entry, and in aremo the schedule pay is being disputed. 2-27-94 fef

properties.Label: Period
properties.Description: The Period is used when aging payment transactions (aret.transcd = 11). Periods 1 - 5 are the age buckets. Period 0 is a future payment. Period 8 is for CODs. Period 9 is for Service Charges. If the service charge was created in ARER then both the aret.transcd 1 record and the corresponding aret.transcd 11 record will have an aret.period of 9. If the service charge was created in ARET then the aret.transcd 1 record will have an aret.period of 0 and the corresponding aret.transcd 11 record will have an aret.period of 9. The possible values for aret.period are 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, and 9.

The Paid-In-Full Dollar Amount holds any writeoff amount when an invoice is considered paid-in-full, yet the applied amount does not equal the payment amount less the discount. If a limit is specified in SASO0: "Cash Rcpts Writeoff Lmt" (sasoo.arwrtofflim) the aret.pifamt cannot exceed this limit. Otherwise it must not exceed the limit specified in ARAO: "Paid in Full Allowance for Cash Receipts" (sasc.arpiflimit). While the aret.pifamt for the individual payment (transcd = 11) holds the writeoff amount for just that transaction, the aret.pifamt for the originating transaction, (transcd = 0-Invoice or 1-Service Charge or 4-C.O.D.) will accumulate the writeoff amounts for all the associated payments. For example a total invoice for $100 has two payments of $50 each, but is paid off with $48 and $49. Each aret for the payments will have an aret.pifamt of $2 and $1 respectively. But, the aret for the invoice will have an aret.pifamt of $3.

Type 1-Service Charges and the corresponding type 11-Payment records created in ARER will contain "On Balance of" and the amount the service charge was calculated on. properties.Label: Geo Code
properties.Description: Taxware Sales and Use Tax (SUT) uses the geo code to determine which taxes should be applied if there is more than one taxing jurisdiction within a zip code. Examples of this are when a zip code crosses county lines and each county has a different tax rate or when multiple cities exist in the same zip code and each city has a different tax rate. Each taxing jurisdiction within the zip code is given a unique, two-digit identifier. Taxware uses the city name, state, zip code and geo code to find the correct tax rates. Taxware Enterprise (TWE) uses the geo code as a unique identifier of a taxing jurisdiction and not a supplemental identifier as in SUT. With TWE, all jusrisdictions world-wide have a geo code. Each geo code can include country, state or province, county, city and district taxing jurisdictions. Any taxing jurisdiction except country can be omitted from the definition of a geo code. TWE can apply the correct tax rates based on the geo code alone. Content:

properties.Label: Order Rep 1 Percent
properties.Description: This field stores an additional order rep percentage that can be assigned to an order. Setups in ARSC will copy to ARSS on a copy and can use the AO logic to copy to ARSS if ARSC is changed (SXE-2803). When an order is created, OEEH defaults from ARSC/ARSS and then OEEL defaults from OEEH. The operator can update the assignments in OEEH/OEEL for individual order/line specifics. Once the data is stored in the OEEH/OEEL records in the database, it will be sent to DataLake and any analysis/calculations (usually for commissions) against these fields will be done in Birst. There are five of these fields that can be used. Note that the field number must match to the ordrep field number, i.e., if ordrep2 is assigned a value and you want a percentage related to that, the percentage must be specified in orderreppct2, the 2 must match on both fields to correlate them. properties.Label: Credit Manager
properties.Description: The initials of the credit manager for the group. The credit manager is the person who is responsible for obtaining credit reports, maintaining and updating credit information, and approving credit when requested by the group. If loaded, the credit notification will be sent to the group credit mananger as well as the credit manager for the customer in the group placing the order. If not loaded, only the customer's credit manager will receive the credit notification. Content:

properties.Label: Credit Limit
properties.Description: The amount of credit extended by the distributor to the group. This value is compared against the total balance plus the on order balance plus the future order balance when determining if an order should be placed on hold. The arsg.credlimappty field will control how the credit limit is applied. If the credit limit is to be controlled by the group, the outstanding balance of all group members will be compbined and compared against the group credit limit. The credit limit values on ARSC or ARSS for group members will not be used. If the group credit limit is to be used as part of a hierarchy, the outstanding balance of the individual group member will be compared first against the group credit limit value. If the order does not go on hold based on the group credit limit, the outstanding balance of the member will be compagred against their ARSC or ARSS credit limit. If the group credit limit is to be bypassed, the outstanding balance of the individual member will only be compared against their credit limit from either ARSC or ARSS. Content:

properties.Label: Credit Limit Apply Type
properties.Help: Indicates How the Group Credit Limit Should Be Applied
properties.Description: Determines how the group credit limit value should be applied with regards to the members of the group. Apply Group Limit - If the credit limit is to be controlled by the group, the outstanding balance of all group members will be compbined and compared against the group credit limit. The credit limit values on ARSC or ARSS for group members will not be used. Group In Hierarchy - If the group credit limit is to be used as part of a hierarchy, the outstanding balance of the individual group member will be compared first against the group credit limit value. If the order does not go on hold based on the group credit limit, the outstanding balance of the member will be compared against their ARSC or ARSS credit limit. Bypass To Customer - If the group credit limit is to be bypassed, the outstanding balance of the individual member will only be compared against their credit limit from either ARSC or ARSS. Content:

properties.Label: Geo Code
properties.Description: Taxware Sales and Use Tax (SUT) uses the geo code to determine which taxes should be applied if there is more than one taxing jurisdiction within a zip code. Examples of this are when a zip code crosses county lines and each county has a different tax rate or when multiple cities exist in the same zip code and each city has a different tax rate. Each taxing jurisdiction within the zip code is given a unique, two-digit identifier. Taxware uses the city name, state, zip code and geo code to find the correct tax rates. Taxware Enterprise (TWE) uses the geo code as a unique identifier of a taxing jurisdiction and not a supplemental identifier as in SUT. With TWE, all jusrisdictions world-wide have a geo code. Each geo code can include country, state or province, county, city and district taxing jurisdictions. Any taxing jurisdiction except country can be omitted from the definition of a geo code. TWE can apply the correct tax rates based on the geo code alone. Content:

properties.Label: Hold Period
properties.Help: If Period Balance Exists, All New Orders Will Be Placed On Hold
properties.Description: The hold period indicates an OE order should be placed on hold if the customer has a balance in the specified period or a later period. A non-zero hold period indicates that the group hold period will take precedence over any hold period at the customer level. If the group member has a balance in the group hold period or later, orders for that group member will go on hold. A zero hold period indicates that the hold period check will not be applied to any member of the group. No OE order for a group member will go on hold based on the hold period A blank hold period indicates that the group should be bypassed and the hold period set up on the individual group member's customer record should be used to determine whether or not the OE order should be placed on hold. properties.Label: Sales Order Status
properties.Description: Determines the approval status of orders entered in OEET by a member of the group. If the group sell type is set to Y - YES, all orders entered by members of the group will be approved if within all other credit parameters If the group sell type is set to N - NO, members of the group will not be allowed to enter orders in OEET. If the group sell type is set to C - CASH ONLY, The only payment type accepted for any member of the group will be cash. If the group sell type is set to D - COD ONLY, the only orders the members of the group can place willb e Cash On Delivery. If the group sell type is set to H - HOLD UNTIL, all orders placed by members of the group will be placed on hold until the group Hold Date is reached. Once the group's hold date has been reached, all new orders will be approved. If the group sell type is set to O - OPEN UNTIL, all orders placed by members of the group will follow the normal credit process until the group Open Date is reached. After that date, all new orders placed by members of the group will be placed on hold. If the group sell type is blank, the approval status check will bypass the group to the individual members of the group. The Sales Order Status set up on the customer record will be used. Content:

properties.Label: Service Chg
properties.Description: This field will control how service charges are applied to members of the group when their balances are rolled in Accounts Receivable Entry Roll Balances (ARER). If the group setting for service charges is set to Y - Yes, service charges can be applied to all members of the group during processing in ARER If the group setting for service charges is set to N - No, service charges will not be applied to any member of the group during processing in ARER. If the group setting for service charges is blank, the group will be bypassed and the service charge setting for the individual group members, found on either ARSC or ARSS, will be used. Content:

properties.Label: Hold or Open Date
properties.Help: On Hold Until or Open Credit Until
properties.Description: The status date can be used to store the 'hold until' date or the 'open until' date depending upon how the selltype field is loaded. The date is used to determine if the OE order being created for a member of the group should be placed on hold. If the group sell type is set to H - HOLD UNTIL, all orders placed by members of the group will be placed on hold until the group Hold Date is reached. Once the group's hold date has been reached, all new orders will be approved. If the group sell type is set to O - OPEN UNTIL, all orders placed by members of the group will follow the normal credit process until the group Open Date is reached. After that date, all new orders placed by members of the group will be placed on hold.

properties.Label: Geo Code
properties.Description: Taxware Sales and Use Tax (SUT) uses the geo code to determine which taxes should be applied if there is more than one taxing jurisdiction within a zip code. Examples of this are when a zip code crosses county lines and each county has a different tax rate or when multiple cities exist in the same zip code and each city has a different tax rate. Each taxing jurisdiction within the zip code is given a unique, two-digit identifier. Taxware uses the city name, state, zip code and geo code to find the correct tax rates. Taxware Enterprise (TWE) uses the geo code as a unique identifier of a taxing jurisdiction and not a supplemental identifier as in SUT. With TWE, all jusrisdictions world-wide have a geo code. Each geo code can include country, state or province, county, city and district taxing jurisdictions. Any taxing jurisdiction except country can be omitted from the definition of a geo code. TWE can apply the correct tax rates based on the geo code alone. Content:

properties.Label: Order Rep 1 Percent
properties.Description: This field stores an additional order rep percentage that can be assigned to an order. Setups in ARSC will copy to ARSS on a copy and can use the AO logic to copy to ARSS if ARSC is changed (SXE-2803). When an order is created, OEEH defaults from ARSC/ARSS and then OEEL defaults from OEEH. The operator can update the assignments in OEEH/OEEL for individual order/line specifics. Once the data is stored in the OEEH/OEEL records in the database, it will be sent to DataLake and any analysis/calculations (usually for commissions) against these fields will be done in Birst. There are five of these fields that can be used. Note that the field number must match to the ordrep field number, i.e., if ordrep2 is assigned a value and you want a percentage related to that, the percentage must be specified in orderreppct2, the 2 must match on both fields to correlate them. Added with JIRA SXE-3048/SXWEB-38216. Content:

properties.Label: Lump Bill Amount
properties.Description: The lump bill amount is enterable on either a BL or BR to override the billing amount to the customer. If each suffix should be billed a fixed rate regardless of the delivery of products on each release, the lump bill amount should be used. The invoice in ARET will be created for the lump bill amount when the order is invoiced.

properties.Label: Lump Sum Bill
properties.Description: Indicates if the lump billing amount should be used when invoicing the customer. The flag allows the flexibility to invoice the customer a 0 amount on a particular invoice. Content:

properties.Label: Print Lump Prices
properties.Description: Indicates that lump bill prices should be printed on the invoice. Content:

properties.Label: Notes
properties.Description: Notes flag designating that notes exist for this bid and if they are required notes. Required notes will always display during entry functions. # NOTE: Required notes will NOT display during the entry function of loading an item group. #

properties.Label: Open Initials
properties.Description: Initials of operator who is currently working on a specific bid. The initials will be cleared when the operator "jumps" to another function, "cancels" out of a bid or "GO"/completes a bid. This soft-locking mechanism provides a method of locking others out of a bid without keeping the record in transaction state. # If for any reason openinits are left on a bid (system went down, etc.), the system supervisor "sys", can sign in and clear the initials by entering the bid in BPET and hitting GO. A message will be displayed stating the the bid is now available for use. #

properties.Label: Open To Release
properties.Description: This field indicates if the bid is "open to release". This means that the user may release more than the original quantity on the bid. During the bid awarding function (bpesa), the user may update this field to indicate if the bid release function (bper) will allow the user to release more than what is considered open on each bid line item. Content:

properties.Label: Last Changed By
properties.Description: Tags the record with the login initials of the last operator to update the record. Last update is defined by the operator pressing GO on a setup screen, or by the completion of a transaction in a batch updating process.

properties.Description: The disposition of the order. Content:

properties.Label: Overwrite Existing PDSC
properties.Description: This field indicates if any existing PDSC records (that are created during the bid release process - if that is the type of bid release process being operated) should be overwritten. If an existing PDSC record is on file and this field = yes, then it will be deleted and re-added. If an existing PDSC is on file and this field = no, then it will be ignored and the bid line item will be considered closed. The user has the ability to enter this field at a line item basis when the perform the Price bid release process. Content:

properties.Label: Price Level
properties.Help: Price/Discounting Setup Customer Price Level 0-9 (0 = base)
properties.Description: Price/Discounting Level for bid/customer. # Enterable: Price Bid Ordering screen (BPETHO) Job Bid Ordering screen (BPETJO) # Valdiated: No # If there is no bid level price level entered for the bid, the ARSS price level will be used. If there is not ARSS or the ARSS level is 0, then it will revert to the ARSS price level. #

properties.Label: Price Type
properties.Description: Customer Price type for Price/Discounting. # Enterable: Price Bid Ordering screen (BPETHO) Job Bid Ordering screen (BPETJO) # Validated: Yes, must exist in SASTT. # If there is not pricetype entered for the header, then the ARSS pricetype will be used. If there is no ARSS or if the ARSS pricetype is blank, then it will revert to the ARSC pricetype. #

properties.Label: Promised Date
properties.Description: The date the order was promised to the customer. The customer will request the order on the requested ship date. Due to stock out problems, drop ship lead times, etc .., the promised date is set as an outside service level check. It defaults from the requested ship date and can be overridden. This date is entered during the Job bid release process which will be used to create a new sales order.

properties.Label: Quote #
properties.Description: System-assigned unique identifying number. # Any place that a bid id may be entered, the user has the option of using the quote number by entering "q" followed by the actual quote number. # Using the include {p-bpfind.i} will allow a procedure to find a bid by "q" + quote number or by bid identifier #

properties.Label: Reference
properties.Description: This is the reference that can be specified during the Price bid release process and will be moved to the new PDSC records that will be created. This is a user specified field that will originally default from the Job ID (for a job bid - bpehj.jobid). Content:

properties.Label: Release Process Complete
properties.Description: This field indicates if the bid release screen dialog process has been completed. When the user pressed <CANCEL> or <GO> from the bid release line item screen, then a pop-up window will display to prompt if the release process is complete. This field is used when the user runs the F10 (Update) from the bid release function and enters 'all' for all bids. All bids where the bid release process has been started (bpeh.relprocessfl = yes) and has been completed (relcompfl=yes) for the operator (bpeh.relinit) will be selected for updating. Content:

properties.Label: Release Initials
properties.Description: This is the initials of the operator that has performed the bid release screen dialog. This is used when the F10 (Update) function is run to collect all bids to update (screen bpid = 'all'). Only those bids that have been done by the operator (bpeh.relinit) will be selected for updating.

properties.Label: Release Process
properties.Description: This field indicates if the bid release screen dialog process has been started. Since the user can begin the screen dialog process and then leave to perform another Trend function, this field is critical to know if the screen process has been started. When the user returns to the bid release process for the bid and this flag = yes, then the bid release header screen will not be shown and the bid line items will not have to be prepared for the screen dialog. Content:

properties.Label: Requested Ship Date
properties.Description: The requested ship date of the new sales order to be created from the bid. This is the date the customer would like you to ship the order. Service level analysis can be obtained relative to meeting this date. It defaults to today's date plus the OEAO additional days plus the ICSD cutoff.

properties.Label: Order Type
properties.Help: SO, DO, FO, BL or PD (Pricing Records)
properties.Description: During the bid release process, the transaction type field is determined by the user for a job bid. This describes the kind of order to create: SO - stock order (reserves inventory. Entry into stage 1) DO - direct order (does not reserve inventory. Entry into stage 2). FO - future order (does not reserve inventory. Entry into stage 0. Converted to a SO through OEEPC or OEEPI when the promise date - oeeh.longltdays - sasc.oefutdays - sasc.oereqdays <= today) BL - blanket order (does not reserve inventory. Entry into stage 0. Always a memo order. BR created from BL with the F8 key from OEET or during the bid release process (new field structures - OEEHBR/OEELBR).

label: Active

properties.Label: Active
properties.Description: The active flag will tell the operator if this ICAMU entry has been "handled" or not. If the operator presses GO from the the F6, F7, or F9 screens, or from the main detail line and a change is made, the record will be set to inactive. Content:

label: Buyer

properties.Label: Buyer
properties.Description: The buyer in ICAMU will be loaded based on the ARP vendor/product line for the ICSW record. If there is an ARP vendor/line, the ICSL record will be read and the buyer will be loaded. If no vendor or line exists, the buyer will be blank. Content:

label: Frozen Reason

properties.Label: Frozen Reason
properties.Help: Frozen Reason from ICAMU, Not ICSW
properties.Description: The frozen reason is loaded into ICAMU based on the frozen condition encountered during the ICAMM run. A product will only be frozen for a single reason, but it may qualify for freezing for multiple reasons. Therefore, multiple ICAMU records may exist for a product/whse combination. Content:

label: Product Line

properties.Label: Product Line
properties.Description: This field represents the source product line for the line item. For a stocked product, it defaults from the ICSW ARP product line. If the ICSW product line is blank, the ICAMU product line will be blank. The product line will be loaded during ICAMU even if the arp type is not a vendor arp. Content:

properties.Description: Harmonized System Tariff Code. The HS system uses a logical nomenclature method to categorize goods into approximately 5,000 commodity groups. properties.Label: Carton ID
properties.Description: The carton that the item belongs to. If the order/detail has an exception during Cartonization, then Carton ID is the Order#: "o1234-00 - Exception" Content:

properties.Label: Company
properties.Description: Company Number - sasc.cono Content:

properties.Label: Item Cube
properties.Description: Height x Width x Length of the Item in the box

properties.Label: Exception Message
properties.Description: If an exception is found during cartonization, then the message is stored on the exception carton. The Carton ID is the Order#: "o1234-00 - Exception" and the statusty of the crton record (icecnhdr.statusty) is 'E'. Exceptions can be deleted once corrected via the ICECN 'Delete Packages' function. Repack the item manually, or delete the package if one is created for the order and re-run auto cartonization.

properties.Label: Item Height
properties.Description: Height of the item being packaged. If the unit on the order line is linked to a Product specific ICSEU record and that record is setup to calculate/store dimensions (icseu.cncalcpkgsizefl) to be able to pack that container inside another container. So it is the Height of the Unit (Container) - Case - Box Content:

properties.Label: Header Row Pointer
properties.Description: What Cartons are the Item in Content:

properties.Label: Packing Instructions
properties.Description: Special packing instructions per item Content:

properties.Label: Item Quantity
properties.Description: Quantity from the Order Lines (OE Lines, WT Lines or OE Components) Not Stocking, but based on the Order Line Unit

properties.Label: Item Unit
properties.Description: Unit from the Order Lines (OE Lines, WT Lines or OE Components)

properties.Label: Item Cube Size
properties.Description: The dimensional Cube Size of the item in the carton. This is used when comparing the Items to put in the carton. How much of the items will fit Cubic Feet Dimension. Height, Width, Length of the carton are measured in Inches, Feet, Yards, Centimeters or Milimeters. Those dimensions are all convered to inches and multiplied together and divided by 1728 to get the cubic feet dimension to be used to see what can fit into the carton dimensionally Content:

properties.Label: Item Length
properties.Description: Length of the item being packaged. If the unit on the order line is linked to a Product specific ICSEU record and that record is setup to calculate/store dimensions (icseu.cncalcpkgsizefl) to be able to pack that container inside another container. So it is the Length of the Unit (Container) - Case - Box Content:

properties.Label: Line#
properties.Description: Line Number of the item being packaged Content:

properties.Label: Order Type
properties.Description: Currrently OE and WT orders can be Cartonized Content:

properties.Label: Order Row Pointer
properties.Description: Links to the order for the item. Multiple orders can be placed into the same carton based on the Ship To, carrier, customer and the Mixed Order setting (icsd.cnmixbyshiptofl) as well as restriction settings and allowing item to be mixed or not. Content:

properties.Label: Product
properties.Description: Item off the order that is in the carton Content:

properties.Label: Row Pointer
properties.Description: Generated GUID Unique identifer of the record

properties.Label: Seq#
properties.Description: If the OE line is a BOD Kit item, then this is the OEELK Sequence Number Content:

properties.Label: Last Change
properties.Description: Server Date, Time, Seconds and Time Zone If WebUI Cloud server will be UTC (time zone 0). On Premise server will be the time zone of the server location.

properties.Label: Trans Proc
properties.Description: Where the record was last updated

properties.Label: Item Weight
properties.Description: Weight of the item being packaged. If the unit on the order line is linked to a Product specific ICSEU record and that record is setup to calculate/store dimensions (icseu.cncalcpkgsizefl) to be able to pack that container inside another container. So it is the Weight of the Unit (Container) - Case - Box Content:

properties.Label: Warehouse
properties.Description: ICSD Cartonization Warehouse or OEEH Warehouse/WTEH Ship From Warehouse if the Customer is setup to use Cartonization and the actual warehouse is not. The Customer from WT orders would be the Direct Order WT orders. Content:

properties.Label: Item Width
properties.Description: Width of the item being packaged. If the unit on the order line is linked to a Product specific ICSEU record and that record is setup to calculate/store dimensions (icseu.cncalcpkgsizefl) to be able to pack that container inside another container. So it is the Width of the Unit (Container) - Case - Box Content:

properties.Label: Actual Weight (Billable)
properties.Description: This is the Actual Weight for the package which is entered in ICECN during the Shipping process of the Packages. There are three weights on the package Actual Dimensional Package

properties.Label: Carton ID
properties.Description: Carton ID of the Package being Shipped. See the different 'Format' options from AO and ICSD. There can be up to four different sections to a Carton ID, or just one. The company can determine what to use and in what position. Sections can be: Whse Package Type Carton Number Additional Lettering If the order/detail has an exception during Cartonization, then Carton ID is the Order#: "o1234-00 - Exception"

properties.Label: Carton Number
properties.Description: The carton number is a system generated number from a database sequence trigger. Incremental. This is the only section of the Carton ID that is required. We store the carton number on the package.

properties.Label: Company
properties.Description: Company Numer - SASC Content:

properties.Label: Dimensional Weight Divisor
properties.Description: Transportation Standard Carrier - Extended Screen Dimensional Weight Divisor. Used with a carrier to determine the minimum weight per box to use for lighter shipments. It will use the Dimensional Weight if it is higher than the actual weight of a box for the billable weight of the package. Cartons Dimensional Cubic Feet / Dimensional Divisor Content:

properties.Label: Dimensional Weight
properties.Description: Cartons Dimensional Cubic Feet / Dimensional Divisor Compared to the Actual Weight of the Package. It will default in the Dimensional Weight if the Dimensional Weight is more. Prevents lighter items shipping with fright changes that are too low

properties.Label: Free Freight
properties.Description: The package can be flagged as a 'Free' shipping package. A promotional shipment or special deal. Loaded as 'free' manaully in ICECN when shipping the Cartons - where Freight and Actual Weight is entered.

properties.Label: Package Freight Amount
properties.Description: The freight charge that is associated with the Package based on the packages actual and dimensional weight. Loaded during the shipping process cartons.

properties.Label: Package Instructions
properties.Description: These are the instructions pulled from the Carton Setup - ICSCN for the specific package being used. Stored on the record for display of the carton instructions or use in Package Labels if the customer want's them to display. Content:

properties.Label: Package Cube Size
properties.Description: The dimensional Cube Size of the carton - not the items in the carton, but the carton itself. This is used when comparing the Items to put in the carton. How much of the items will fit Cubic Feet Dimension. Height, Width, Length of the carton are measured in Inches, Feet, Yards, Centimeters or Milimeters. Those dimensions are all convered to inches and multiplied together and divided by 1728 to get the cubic feet dimension to be used to see what can fit into the carton dimensionally

properties.Label: Package Group
properties.Description: When a package is a special package and links to specific items, then the Package Group Type can be used to group specific items together in a specific package. Dry Ice container Drum for liquid Content:

properties.Label: Package ID
properties.Description: This is the ICSCN (Carton Setup) Package ID. Shows the operator during picking/shipping which Package to use to pack the items listed in the Detail Carton (ICECNDTL) records. Content:

properties.Label: Package Number
properties.Description: This links the Package to an OEEHP record package number. OEEHP records are created from the Shipping interface, but are numeric numbers. Cartonization packages are based on Carton ID's. Initially, the only way to link an external shipped package to a Cartonization Package is manaully entering the Package Number from the Shipping Interface to the Package in ICECN during the Shipping of the Carton - when entering the Weight and Freigh charges. It can be an informaitonal field that is manually entered during the shipping process in ICECN and not be linked to OEEHP records at all.

properties.Label: Package Type
properties.Description: This is a way to link specific types of packages to specific types of items. There is a package type stored on the ICSP/ICSC records. If those are loaded, they can only be packaged into cartons of the same package type The Package stored the Package Type on the carton so the opertor can see what types of items are in the carton. Content:

properties.Label: Package Weight
properties.Description: This is the combined weight of all the items in the package. This is the weigh totalled from the ICSP Weight (Stocking) converted to the unit conversion on the line of the order and then multipled by the quantity in the box for the item. A system generated weight. This will default in as the weight during shipping of the package, but the opertor will enter in the Actual Weight of the package to be compared to the Dimensional Weight. The system weight is used during cartonization to find packages and compare to package min/max weight settings.

properties.Label: Row Pointer
properties.Description: System generated GUID Unique identifier of the record Loads in the Detail Carton record - icecndtl.icecnhdrrowpointer to show what cartons all the items are connected to

properties.Label: Shipment ID
properties.Description: The operator can select to manually enter a Shipping ID to be attached to the Cartons via ICECN - when running Auto Cartonization. The operator can enter in an ASN Number, a Truck Number. The ID is a way to link all the orders in the Cartonization process together. An easy way in ICECN to see all the cartons for a Shipment - Advance Search. If a Shipping ID is chosen to be created automatically (from ICECN or the Picking runs - OEEPP/WTEP), it will be in the following format: YYYYMMDD-HH:MM:SS-zz9

properties.Label: Size Measurement of Package
properties.Description: What is the measurement of the package in. Pulled from the ICSCN Package setup Content:

properties.Label: Carton Status

properties.Label: Whse
properties.Description: Records the warehouse of receipts or returns.

properties.Label: Company #
properties.Description: Identifies the Company under which the record was created.

properties.Label: Cost
properties.Description: This is the cost as is occurs on this individual record. It corresponds to the G/L entry for this specific record. As such, it will include add-ons if capitalizing them (incoming through PO) or if included in SM/GL cost (outgoing). The cost is always in domestic currency, is always in stocking units, and always represents a per unit cost, to be matched with the units on the record. If the item is a special price/cost item (see ICSP), the cost on the ICET record will represent the cost per special price/cost unit, not per stocking unit. This is referred to as the 'raw' cost.

properties.Label: Customer #
properties.Description: Customer number, as in Trend Standard. Present only on records that relieve inventory through Order Entry or on returned goods through Order Entry. It is validated against ARSC.

properties.Label: Division #
properties.Description: The division number of the warehouse affected by the transaction. In most situations, this division will be the same as the ICSD division. You can, however, choose to have the division number loaded from the customer record. In this case ICET records that are associated with customer transactions will be loaded with the division number from the customer record. All other cases and all other settings will produce a division number matching that of ICSD. This is the recommended use of the the field.

properties.Label: Entered
properties.Description: The creation date of the record. This is set to be equal to the variable 'g-today'. This global variable always equals the current system date except when scheduled reports go past midnight, in which case it represents the date when the report should have run.

properties.Label: Spec Rec Link
properties.Help: Special Price/Cost Record Number for Link to Transactions
properties.Description: This field will identify the special price/costing data that is related to this record. This number can be matched up to the ICSS record with the primary unique key k-icss. NOTE: This field is a decimal field with zero decimals. All of the other icspecrecno fields, with the exception of the icetl, icets, icetf, and icet files, are integer fields. Care should be taken to ensure the integretity of the data.

properties.Label: ICSW Cost
properties.Description: This represents the SM/GL as it existed BEFORE the application of the current posting function (the one creating this record). If appropriate, this includes the average add-on figure. This field is very important as it represents the only way of figuring a cost for the valuation of inventory for an 'as of' trial balance. The ICRT report uses this figure from the first record posted AFTER the cutoff date to calculate total value. It is critical that every ICET record create record this figure prior to any recalculations. If the product is a special price/cost item (see ICSP) then this cost is in the special price/cost unit, not the stocking unit. This is called the 'raw' cost.

properties.Label: Jrnl #
properties.Description: journal #

properties.Label: Line#
properties.Description: Line Number is the line number from the supporting document for this transaction. The use will vary depending on the document type. It is a valid field only for those transactions created from a document (OE,PO, etc.)

properties.Label: Merged
properties.Description: The Merged flag is used to control updates to ICSWU from ICAM. This flag is set to 'no' by all procedures that create ICET and is set to 'yes' by the ICAM process itself.

properties.Label: Module
properties.Description: This represents the Trend module that created the ICET transaction. IT follows the Trend 'ouproc' name, not 'currproc'. It is important that 'ourproc' is used to ensure that reports and inquiries can find the proper record regardless of source. As users invent their own SASSM entries it is important that ICET.MODULE remain something that standard Trend programs can identify.

properties.Label: Notes
properties.Description: Notes Flag to track if a note exists on a specific ICET record. Content:

properties.Label: Notes ID
properties.Help: Unique ID for Notes Creation to a Specific ICET Record
properties.Description: This is an incremetal number that is generated from a 'Sequence' in the ICET record called icetnotesid. As a note is attached to a specific ICET record, the sequence is created and used as the unique connection to the NOTES record and the ICET record. Since ICET does not have a primary/unique index, the sequence id is required to keep the link specific to the records. Content:

properties.Label: Last Change By
properties.Description: Tags the record with the login initials of the last operator to update the record. Last update is defined by the operator pressing GO on a setup screen, or by the completion of a transaction in a batch updating process.

properties.Label: Order #
properties.Description: The document number from the document that created the ICET. This will vary depending on the document (if any). Document numbers come from: OE, PO, WT, KP As needed, order numbers are generated from IC postings in certain situations. These are needed on serial/lot and warehouse manager controlled items for updating purposes.

properties.Label: Order Suffix
properties.Description: See orderno. This is the suffix, if any, for the orderno field. If an orderno is used for ICET the order suffix will also be assigned.

properties.Label: Orig Cost

properties.Label: Phy Adj Excpt
properties.Description: This field is used to indicate problems or warnings that occured during the posting of physical or cycle count adjustments. They are used in ICEJ to provide warnings to the user or reviewer of the postings made to perpetual inventory. Content:

properties.Label: Date
properties.Description: The posting date is from the posting date of the journal. It will always match the GLET entry for the ICET information, allowing an as-of trial balance.

properties.Label: Product #

properties.Label: Unavailable
properties.Description: This field is used for reference purposes only. It indicates if any of the stockqtyship value will be moved to unavailable. The actual transaction that performs the move is in another ICET transaction, type "UN". Note that this field is not used by all Trend procedures and may be dropped from a future release.

This field can be traced directly to quantity on hand in most situtations. Note that on a type RE transaction it is possible to update the 'received' figure instead of the 'on-hand' figure. This is done if backorder fill will be run to fill existing orders prior to releasing stock for sale. This capability can be seen in PO, WT, and KP (any process that runs back order fill). Stock is moved to on-hand as it is used to fill back orders. Any stock remaining after back order fill is moved to on-hand to fill new orders.

properties.Label: Usage Product

In most cases the value of usageprod will be the same as icet.prod. But if a substitute occurs, icet.prod will contain the substituted product which was actually sold (or transferred) and usageprod will contain the original product which was substituted. During the icam run, the usage will be added to the original product that is stored in this field.

If the product is a special price/cost item (see ICSP) then this cost is in the special price/cost unit, not the stocking unit. This is called the 'raw' cost.

properties.Description: The Merged flag is used to control updates to ICSWU from ICAM. This flag is set to 'no' by all procedures that create ICET and is set to 'yes' by the ICAM process itself.

properties.Description: This represents the Trend module that created the ICET transaction. IT follows the Trend 'ouproc' name, not 'currproc'. It is important that 'ourproc' is used to ensure that reports and inquiries can find the proper record regardless of source. As users invent their own SASSM entries it is important that ICET.MODULE remain something that standard Trend programs can identify.

properties.Label: Quantity
properties.Description: This records the affect on inventory of this particular transaction, up or down. The quantity is always in stocking units. This field can be traced directly to quantity on hand in most situtations. Note that on a type RE transaction it is possible to update the 'received' figure instead of the 'on-hand' figure. This is done if backorder fill will be run to fill existing orders prior to releasing stock for sale. This capability can be seen in PO, WT, and KP (any process that runs back order fill). Stock is moved to on-hand as it is used to fill back orders. Any stock remaining after back order fill is moved to on-hand to fill new orders.

properties.Label: Usage Product
properties.Description: This field will be blank if icet.usagefl is set to "no". If icet.usagefl is set to "yes", usageprod will be the product whose usage is updated during icam. properties.Label: Maximum Cube Percent
properties.Description: When a Carton is created, the ICSD (Warehouse) defaults setting, if loaded for the Maximum Cube Percent will default into the Package value. The Maximum Cube Percent cannot be less than or equal to the Minimum Cube Percent if the Min value is loaded. If the Maximum Cube Percent is zero, then it is assumed that the Package does not have a maximum cube limit. Content:

properties.Label: Maximum Weight
properties.Description: Items total weight cannot exceed this max weight for the package The Maximum Weight value cannot be less than or equal to the Minimum Weight if the Minimum Weight setting is loaded (not Zero). If the Maximum Weight on the packages is Zero, then there is assumed to not be a weight limit on the package. The weight is always measured in pounds. Content:

properties.Label: Minimum Cube Percent
properties.Description: When a Carton is created, the ICSD (Warehouse) defaults setting, if loaded for the Minimum Cube Percent will default into the Package value. The Minimum Cube Percent cannot be greater than or equal to the Maximum Cube Percent if the Max value is loaded. If the Minimum Cube Percent is zero, then it is assumed that the Package does not have a minimum cube requirement. This in the Fill Percentage - Cube Capacity that is required to use this package which prevents sending out a box that is not full Content:

properties.Label: Minimum Weight
properties.Description: Items total weight must meet this minimum to use the carton this carton. If the amount is 0, then the system assumes there is no Minimum Weight requirement for the package. The minimum cannot exceed the Maximum Weight of the package if the Maximum Weight carries a value other than Zero. The weight is always measured in pounds. Content:

The new field will be used to control the Auto WT Receiving that can happen during the shipment of a WT via WTES (Char or GUI) or WLEBS. This option cannot be set if the ICSD Whse is a Whse Logistics Whse. That is why it sits next to the WL Location field. The option is also independant of Direct Orders. If the option is set to yes, then the outbound BOD will send the Header and Detail information that is attached to the order. It uses the same Node structure that was put in place with the TWL project and sending carton informaiton outbound. The difference is the data sent is not based on OEEHP records, but off ICECNHDR and ICSCNDTL record information on the order. Content:

The Package Type is loaded on each Package in the system. In SASTT, there is a Package Type setup. It allows the used of the full Package Type defined (ength up to 8) and connected to the Package, or the SASTT setup can allow for up to three characters Example: Full Type = Dry Ice Carton ID = DI Content:

properties.Description: Both cnusecartonidfl and cnctnletterfl have to be turned on to use this setting When using the letter code in the Carton ID, the system starts the Letter Coce as 'AA' and will increment with each carton it is used in. ie - AA, AB, AC, AD . . . . to ZZ, then starts over. It is an updatable field, but will show in ICSD, the last Letter Code used by the system.

It is a sequentially system generated number that is always used in the Carton ID, but the formatting allows selection of where the number displays in the sections used. There is a similar setting on the Customer record to allow for more specific use of the outbound data and larger customers that require carton detaill on the invoices. Content:

label: Mix Multiple Orders Same Ship To

properties.Label: Mix Multiple Orders Same Ship To
properties.Description: If set to no, then the order processing for cartons is by individual orders. properties.Label: Geo Code
properties.Description: Taxware Sales and Use Tax (SUT) uses the geo code to determine which taxes should be applied if there is more than one taxing jurisdiction within a zip code. Examples of this are when a zip code crosses county lines and each county has a different tax rate or when multiple cities exist in the same zip code and each city has a different tax rate. Each taxing jurisdiction within the zip code is given a unique, two-digit identifier. Taxware uses the city name, state, zip code and geo code to find the correct tax rates. Taxware Enterprise (TWE) uses the geo code as a unique identifier of a taxing jurisdiction and not a supplemental identifier as in SUT. With TWE, all jusrisdictions world-wide have a geo code. Each geo code can include country, state or province, county, city and district taxing jurisdictions. Any taxing jurisdiction except country can be omitted from the definition of a geo code. TWE can apply the correct tax rates based on the geo code alone. Content:

Height is required if the option is on. Unit that is measured dimensionally can be shipped as is, or packed into another carton, but need the dimensions to pack the unit (Case, Box, etc) Content:

properties.Label: Package Length
properties.Description: This is used with cncalcpkgsizefl. If using the dimensional values of the unit to pack cartons with, then need to know what dimension the 'unit' is being measured in. Length is required if the option is on. Unit that is measured dimensionally can be shipped as is, or packed into another carton, but need the dimensions to pack the unit (Case, Box, etc) Content:

properties.Label: Shelf to Ship Stocking UOM
properties.Description: Is this unit self contained in a carton that can be shipped 'as is'. If they order the unit 'case' or 'crate' or 'box' or 'pallet', etc then the item can be pulled from the shelf. Put on a Carton ID, Shipping Label and it can be weighed with a feight charge assigned and shipped. Content:

properties.Label: Tare Weight
properties.Description: This is used with cncalcpkgsizefl. If using the dimensional values of the unit to pack cartons with, then need to know what dimension the 'unit' is being measured in. Not required, but this is the weight of the empty unit - Box, Case Unit that is measured dimensionally can be shipped as is, or packed into another carton, but need the dimensions to pack the unit (Case, Box, etc) Adds the weight of the items in the unit to the weight of the unit to get the total weight of the unit. Content:

properties.Label: Package Type
properties.Description: Package Type. Links to the SASTT Package Type setup table. The Unit package type becomes the carton package type when processing the carton (unit) as a shelf to shipment container. The Package Type carries a 'Carton ID' value for the Carton ID creation for the carton. If packing the Unit into other cartons, then the Package Type becomes the item package type to be used for packing restrictions or mixing item, etc Content:

properties.Label: Package Width
properties.Description: This is used with cncalcpkgsizefl. If using the dimensional values of the unit to pack cartons with, then need to know what dimension the 'unit' is being measured in. Width is required if the option is on. Unit that is measured dimensionally can be shipped as is, or packed into another carton, but need the dimensions to pack the unit (Case, Box, etc) Content:

properties.Label: Size Measurement of Unit
properties.Description: This is used with cncalcpkgsizefl. If using the dimensional values of the unit to pack cartons with, then need to know what dimension the 'unit' is being measured in If blank, it uses the AO option for Cartonization system measurement of Packages. Content:

table_description: Catalog Group Keys - This table serves a dual purpose. The first purpose is to create an environment in which a store can easily add products to a branch of a tree or create a branch without having to know the specific nodeid for that node on the tree. This will be accomplished by using a tag that is specific to each store or by using a product which has already been placed on the tree as a reference product. The second purpose is to allow us to report on and manage the store specific tree structure.

properties.Label: Push
properties.Help: Push From Central Whse or Satellite Pulls From Central Whse
properties.Description: Authorized Replenishment Path Push Flag. This flag is used only if the the ARP is from another location, not if from vendor. A true value indicates that the supplying location will push product to the the receiving location (this branch). A false indicates that the receiving location (this location) will request product when needed from the supplying branch. Note that this flag is the default for ICSW if vendor/line is provided.

properties.Label: Authorized Replenishment Path

properties.Description: This field indicates whether or not freight is expected for purchase orders with this product line. Content:

properties.Label: Frozen Months
properties.Help: Warning: Frozen Months Should Not be Changed (8632)
properties.Description: Indicates the number of months frozen. This field can be set by either the user or the computer (through ICAM). This field is used by ICAM to determine when the product should be 'unfrozen' and brought back into the ICAM calculation loop. If set to '99' (the system will never set to this) the product will be considered frozen forever.

properties.Label: Frozen Reason
properties.Description: The frozen type corresponds to table entries in SASTT, Type 'F'. It should be used by the user to freeze a product.

properties.Label: Freight Consolidation Code
properties.Description: This field indicates what type of products within the product line will automatically be sent to eSource in an eSource Request when POERR is processed It will provide for a way of “consolidating” purchase orders. The “Freight Consolidation Code” will be used to select all purchase orders with the same ICSL freight consolidation code in POERA

properties.Label: Avg Lead Time
properties.Description: The average lead time for this product in days. This is calculated automatically by any receiving function. The average is calculated across the current receipt, the last receipt, and the previous receipt. If a lead time is more than six months old the average is not calculated.

properties.Label: Line Point/Max
properties.Description: Line Point for ordering controls. For most ordering types, the line point is the point where RRAR will pick up this item for reordering providing the line is already in a review state. This field is set by ICAM using standard Gordon Graham methods. If the ordering type is min/max, this field is used to store the maximum stock point.

properties.Label: Review Days
properties.Help: # of Days Ahead of Season to Review Product for Purchase
properties.Description: Number of seasonal review days. This indicates the number of days prior to season begin for preseason buying. It is used by the seasonal analysis report (ICRIP) to bring the product to the buyer's attention at the appropriate time to conduct pre-season buys. It is user input and maintained.

properties.Label: Last Change By
properties.Description: Tags the record with the login initials of the last operator to update the record. Last update is defined by the operator pressing GO on a setup screen, or by the completion of a transaction in a batch updating process.

properties.Label: Order Method
properties.Description: The order calculate type determines the method to be used in calculating the quantity to order when this product needs to be ordered. It is used by ICAM to determine and set the order quantity. Note that it is not used by RRAR except in the case of Min/Max. Order quantities are calculated dynamically for Min/Max. This field also appears on a large number of IC and PO reports. Content:

properties.Label: Order Point/Min
properties.Description: Order Point. This is the basic quantity used by RRAR functions to determine when to order product. It is calculated by ICAM and includes safety stock. The calculation is usage during the ordering period (determined by lead time) plus safety stock. For example: 30 used per month 10 days lead time 50% safety stock Used during lead time = 10 (one per day for ten days lead time) Safety Stock = 5 (50% of usage during lead time or 10) Order Point = 15

properties.Label: Order Qty
properties.Description: Order Quantity. This is the quantity that RRAR will use when ordering this product. If will be used for all types except Min/Max. If the item is seasonal this field is the in season quantity. If the item is not seasonal this is the only quantity used.

properties.Label: RRAR < 1/2 Unit Rounding
properties.Description: Can have 2 values: Blank or "U". When it is "U" and the order quantity is less than 1/2 a standard pack,then POERR will round the order quantity UP to 1 standard pack. If it is blank then no rounding occurs(i.e. still processes as did before t26436).

properties.Label: Surplus Type
properties.Help: A)ctual Monthly Usage or I)CSW Usage Rate (Blank Same as I)
properties.Description: The default method for calculation of surplus. This value will default onto new ICSW records that are created with the given product line. The value will be used in ICRIS during the surplus calculations if specified. Content:

properties.Label: HS Code
properties.Description: Harmonized System Tariff Code. The HS system uses a logical nomenclature method to categorize goods into approximately 5,000 commodity groups. Countries often assign customs duties based on the harmonized tariff code of the product. Used as part of the hierachy to load the HS tariff code on an OE line or PO line for a nonstock product. properties.Label: Manually Pack Item
properties.Description: Items that require special attention while packing. There is something unique about the item and a person needs to pack this item. It may be a really long or extra heavy item. Could be linked to a Group Type on the Package if a special package is required Will not be included in the Automatic cartonization process based on the cubic dimension of the item. Content:

properties.Label: Packing Instructions
properties.Description: Based on the Group Types or Special Item, there may be a need to attach special packing/shipping instructions for the item. There are instructions on the Package Setup record per package as well. These instructions are stored on the Carton Detail record if they exist for the item.

properties.Label: Packing Group Type List
properties.Description: Packing Restriction field (icsp.cnpkgrestrictty) must be 'Group Type Only' to allow selection of a Type Allows for No Selection, One Selection or Multiple Selections The auto cartonization function will match the types based on the 'most' items with the same types. Not always all types, but matching types to other items and packages. Content:

properties.Label: Packing Restriction
properties.Description: Do Not Mix: No specific types are required, but this Item must be packed alone Group Type Only: Links items into cartons based on the Package Group types entered. Types on the item, must match to the types on the Package. Blank: No restrictions, this is the Default. A standard item can be packed with any other standard items Content:

properties.Label: Shelf to Ship Stocking UOM
properties.Description: Yes - Excluded from Cartonization. Assumes in shipping package already (box, case, pallet). No need to package the item. Ships in the container of the unit on the order. The Order line UOM must match the ICSP Stocking Unit of Measure to be considered a Shelf to Ship item during Cartonization If using auto cartonization, the system will assign a Carton ID per package quantity on the order (1 of 5) Assumes the Stocking Unit on the ICSP record is in a Carton not an Each Content:

properties.Label: Package Type
properties.Description: Not a required field. When an item is a standard item, that can use any Standard Package type carton, then there is no need to add a Package Type or Special Package type setting. When the type is loaded, then the item can only be packaged in those similar types of packages. Content:

properties.Label: Size Measurement of Item
properties.Description: This field is used in determining the measurement of the Item’s Height, Weight, and Length. Converts measurements to Dimensional Cubic Feet Compares the size of the item to the dimensional cubic feet size of the packages to determine the packages to usevduring the cartonization process. Content:

properties.Label: Intrastat Commodity Code
properties.Description: Used in the Intrastat procesing of an item - this is the Commodity Code for the item. The commodity code is validated against the SASTT setup values and is sent to ADP to help in the intrastat processing of data. This field is required for Intrastat processing to determine what items to send data to ADP, Content:

properties.Label: Company #
properties.Description: Identifies the Company under which the record was created.

properties.Label: Core Charge
properties.Description: The standard core charge, if any, for this product. The core charge will be charged to the customer on any sale. It can be overridden from the extented screen (F7) in Order Entry. During a return, the customer can be credited with the product charge (price), the core charge, or both. Core charges are used as a deposit-like system in two situations: 1) When buying a rebuilt item (electric motors for example) where the old, defective item will be rebuilt and resold. 2) When buying something that requires a returnable container, such as gases in a tank. The customer is charge for both the item and the core. When the old item or the container is returned, the customer gets a core credit.

properties.Label: Country of Origin
properties.Description: The country in which a product was manufactured, produced, or grown. Used as part of the hierachy to load the country of origin on an OE line or PO line for a nonstock product. Used to load a default country of origin on a new ICSW record. Content:

properties.Label: Cube
properties.Description: The size, in cubes, represented by a single stocking unit of this particular item. This field is generally for user information, printing on pick tickets and a few reports. There are two situations, however, where the value of this field becomes important: 1) Order Targets by Cube. Cube can be used as a target method in ICSL. If so, the cube value * the quantity ordered is used for target and minimum buy information. Note also that if target is cube, the total volume in APSP will be by cube and review cycles will be calculated using total cubes and target cubes. 2) If using warehouse manager and calculating bin capacity by cube, this field is used to determine the total quantity of product that can fit in a bin and the space available in any bin containing this product. For this purpose it is important that cube is as accurate as possible.

properties.Label: # Parts
properties.Help: Number of Entry Fields for Cut Allocation Entry, Enter 0 When Not a Cut Part
properties.Description: SXRF Cut Product Number of Parts If the product is set up as a Linear Cut product (icsp.cuttype = L), the length of a cut piece can be entered as one number (feet) or as two numbers (feet and inches). This field indicates how many fields should be displayed to the user when the user is enteing length data. Content:

properties.Label: 2nd Part Increment
properties.Help: Enter the 2nd Part Increment - How Many 2nd Part Units in Each 1st Part
properties.Description: SXRF Cut Product Part Increment #2 If the product is set up as a Linear Cut product (icsp.cuttype = L), the length of a cut piece can be entered as one number (feet) or as two numbers (feet and inches). If the length is entered as two numbers, this field stores the relationship between the two. For example: 12 inches per foot or 100 centimeters per meter Content:

properties.Label: 1st Part Type
properties.Help: Enter the 1st Part Entry Type - (D)ecimal or (I)nteger
properties.Description: SXRF Cut Product Part Type #1 If the product is set up as a Linear Cut product (icsp.cuttype = L), the length of a cut piece can be entered as one number (feet) or as two numbers (feet and inches). This field is used to indicate how the first field should be formatted. The length value can be entered as a whole number (Integer) or it can be entered as a decimal number (Decimal) Content:

properties.Label: 2nd Part Type
properties.Help: Enter the 2nd Part Entry Type - (D)ecimal or (I)nteger
properties.Description: SXRF Cut Product Part Type #2 If the product is set up as a Linear Cut product (icsp.cuttype = L), the length of a cut piece can be entered as one number (feet) or as two numbers (feet and inches). properties.Label: Part 1 Unit
properties.Description: SXRF Cut Product Part Unit #1 If the product is set up as a Linear Cut product (icsp.cuttype = L), the length of a cut piece can be entered as one number (feet) or as two numbers (feet and inches). This field is used to indicate the unit associated with the first field.

properties.Label: Part 2 Unit

properties.Label: Cut Type
properties.Description: This field will indicate whether the product is to be used with the Dimensional Cut functionality in VA (MSF# 186085), whether it is to be used with the Linear Cut functionality in SX RF (MSF# 142967), or whether it is not a cut product. The initial value is that a product is NOT a cut product. Content:

properties.Label: Description

Individual words in the description are also loaded as a part of the keyword system. To best utilize keywords, make sure to put spaces, not punctuation, between the words of the description. For example: GOOD: 1/2" Carbide Drill Bit, 3/8" Shank BAD: 1/2"-Carbide Drillbit-3/8"Shank
