properties.Label: Entered
properties.Description: This date is filled in automatically whenever a product is created either manually or automatically. It appears on various reports and inquiries but is not used internally for any significant functionality.

properties.Label: List Kit on Invoice
properties.Help: List the Kit Components on the Invoice
properties.Description: Explode on Invoice Print Flag. This flag is relevant only for Kit items. If the item is a kit, this controls the invoice print routine. Content:

properties.Label: Exclude from Repricing
properties.Description: Used for Auto Vendor Repricing. When set to yes, the product will be excluded from Auto Vendor Repricing. Default is No

properties.Label: Height
properties.Help: Enter Height of Product; Used to Calculate Cube

properties.Label: Spec Rec Link
properties.Help: Special Price/Cost Record Number for Link to Transactions
properties.Description: This field will identify the special price/costing data that is related to this record. This number can be matched up to the ICSS record with the primary unique key k-icss.

properties.Label: Imply Qty
properties.Description: This field represents the implied quantity ratio. That is, the number of implied cores per each remanufactured core.

properties.Label: Word Index
properties.Description: Internal field used for keyword processing Content:

properties.Label: Non Stock Component Required
properties.Description: The Kit Nonstock Required Flag indicates if the Build on Demand Kit should contain required Non-stock Kit Component(s). While in OE and BP, the Operator is notified if entry of at lease one nonstock is required. In OE, the field is check during the entry process. In BP, the field is checked during the release process. The user is allowed to set the flag to 'yes' for a Prebuilt Kit, but Nonstock Components are not allowed on KP Work Orders. This could be a future enhancement. Content:

properties.Label: OE Kit Rollup
properties.Description: Kit Roll Type. This field is used to control price and cost roll techniques on build on demand kits only. It can be left blank at any time and has no affect on any product type other than build on demand kits. Content:

properties.Label: Kit Type
properties.Help: (P)rebuilt, (B)uild on Demand or Blank if not a Kit
properties.Description: Type of kit, if any. Normally blank, this field is used only for kit products. Prebuilt kits are built using work orders in KPET. A prebuilt kit is expected to be found on the shelf, and the quantity on hand will normally by above zero. Usage is tracked on a prebuilt kit. Build on demand kits are rarely true products on the shelf. Instead, they serve as a 'shorthand' for a collection of products to be gathered and, if appropriate, assembled at shipping time. Availability of build on demand kits is based on the availability of the components. Content:

properties.Label: Length
properties.Help: Enter Length of Product; Used to Calculate Cube

properties.Label: LIFO Category
properties.Description: This field is required if using the Trend LIFO system. Trend LIFO uses a pooled inventory method. LIFO layers are kept for each pool, not for each product. This catagory field determines the LIFO pool for this product. It is validated by a 'Q' entry in SASTT. If not using LIFO, this can be left blank. Note that changing the catagory for a given product DOES NOT ripple back through past year layers. The catagory will not be used until this year's LIFO Valuation.

properties.Label: Lookup Name
properties.Description: The lookupnm is used as a secondary index for the ICSP file (the primary is product). Lookup Name can default from the product id, the first description, or the second description (based on ICAO option). Careful consideration should be given as to the lookup name value. Examples: Good: Bit, 1/4" C Bit, 1/2" C Bit, 1/4" M Bit, 1/2" M Bad: 1/4" C Bit C Bit, 1/2" Bit, M 1/2"

properties.Label: Last MSDS Change
properties.Description: This date is used to record the last time the MSDS information changed for this product. The field is used in conjunction with the sheet # and customer information to determine if a new sheet needs to be sent to the customer. Note: This date must be changed manually. Chaning ICSEH will not change all the products associated with that sheet.

properties.Label: MSDS Product
properties.Description: MSDS Controlled Product. This determines whether or not the item is associated with an MSDS record. If 'yes', sheets or notification will be given whenever the product is sold for the first time to a customer or whenever the msdschgdt field is after the last sale date for a given customer.

properties.Label: MSDS Sheet #
properties.Description: This number ties to the ICSEH records if they are set up. The sheet number is used to record the Material Safety Data Sheet that should be send with this product. The sheet number is NOT validated against ICSEH, so it is possible to use the number simply as reference. It will print on a report or on pick tickets depending on your ICAO settings.

properties.Label: Intrastat Net Mass
properties.Description: Applies to VAT and intrastat processing. It is the Net Mass of an item. If using intrastat processing, the item can use Supplementary Units or Net Mass - one or the otehr is required. Which ever is used is reported to TWE for intrastat reporting. Must be set as ECSales in SASGV and SASTT - Country.

properties.Label: No SPC Default
properties.Help: SPC Record Number For No Special Price/Cost Unit

properties.Label: Notes
properties.Description: Trend Standard. Content:

properties.Label: OE SPC Default
properties.Help: SPC Record Number For Order Entry

properties.Label: Last Change By
properties.Description: Tags the record with the login initials of the last operator to update the record. Last update is defined by the operator pressing GO on a setup screen, or by the completion of a transaction in a batch updating process.

properties.Label: Price Book Sequence#
properties.Description: Price Book Sequence Number. This field is user controlled. Duplicate entries are allowed and the field can be left blank. If used, various price book printouts (in PD) can be printed in price book sequence order.

properties.Label: Multiplier
properties.Description: The Price On Type indicates the standard method of pricing this product to customers. Note that no price is indicated and this field is simply a default. It indicates the normal multiplier method to be used whenever selling this product. Users will usually want to set up an initial value for this field. If multipliers are never used, this field is irrelavent. This field is used by PDSC to set PDSC price on type whenever a new record is created for this product. Content:

properties.Label: Product
properties.Description: This, with cono, is the primary key for the ICSP file. The product id is the main identifier, SKU, or part number for this record. Each entry within a single company must be unique.

properties.Label: Category
properties.Description: Product Category. This field is required and validated against 'C' entries in SASTT. This is usually the primary G/L breakout for inventory, sales and cost of goods sold accounts. Sales manager is usually also stored by prodcat. Many of the inventory and sales manager reports and inquiries can also be directed by prodcat. Two notes: 1) prodcat is NOT the primary control field for ordering. Those fields are in ICSW. 2) prodcat should NOT be changed lightly. If posting SM or GL by prodcat any changes to an established product will have to be accompanied by manual changes to SM and/or GL balances. Changing the prodcat is an easy way to throw inventory out of balance. Content:

properties.Label: Product Tier
properties.Description: This field is optional in ICSP and ICSC. The product tier is set up in SASTT and validated in ICSP and ICSC. Product tiers refer to quality and can be used to group products. Product preference groupings which refer to priority are set up in ICSW. Exceptions can be set up in ICSEE. Content:

properties.Label: Rental Product Category
properties.Description: A separate product category that will be used if the product is stocked in a rental warehouse. The rental product category will be used to find and post to a different set of GL accounts so that rental and sales postings are kept separated. Content:

properties.Label: Row Pointer
properties.Description: A unique identifier that can be used to link other records to this particular record. Content:

properties.Label: Round By
properties.Description: The Selling Multiplier is used to ensure a standard selling quantity in Order Entry. If entered, the product can be sold ONLY in multiples of this number. For example, pipe might be stocked by the foot even though it comes in 20 foot lengths. To ensure that even lengths are always sold, set the selling multiplier to '20'. Order entry will default to 20 and will round up any entered quantity to the next even multiplier. This field is used in Order Entry and in the pricing inquiries OEIP and ICIP.

properties.Label: Seq#
properties.Description: This field is used as an extension of the lookup name field. It is not required but can be used to determine the sort order of items where the lookup name is the same. Example: Lookup Name Seq # Product Ratch Set 001 1/4" Drive Ratchet Set, SAE Ratch Set 002 1/4" Drive Ratchet Set, MET Ratch Set 003 3/8" Drive Ratchet Set, SAE Ratch Set 004 3/8" Drive Ratchet Set, MET

properties.Label: SL Update Date
properties.Help: Date Last Updated Through Supplier Link

properties.Label: Supplier Group
properties.Help: Enter User Defined Product Grouping for Supplier Link

properties.Label: Status
properties.Description: This field determines the status type of the product. It is used throughout Trend for all reports, inquiries, and entry functions. Items appear on the buy list according to their status. Items can be turned off or on for selling or buying by their status. Content:

properties.Label: HS Code
properties.Description: Harmonized System Tariff Code. The HS system uses a logical nomenclature method to categorize goods into approximately 5,000 commodity groups. Countries often assign customs duties based on the harmonized tariff code of the product. Used as part of the hierachy to load the HS tariff code on an OE line or PO line for a nonstock product. Used to load a default HS tariff code on a new ICSW record. Content:

properties.Label: Terms Disc
properties.Help: (Y)es for Default, (N)o for Product Specific Cash Terms
properties.Description: This flag is used for calculating the cash discount for customers whenever this product is sold. There is a long chain of defaults that determine discount calculation. In general, if this flag is 'no', the standard discount percent is used for this customer based on terms type. If, however, the terms allow it and the flag is 'yes', it may be that this line item on an order will receive a zero or modified cash discount. This flag is used if the product is sold without a qualifying PDSC record. This flag is also used as a default for the creation of any PDSC records. If a PDSC record is used during the sale, the setting of this flag in PDSC overrides the ICSP setting. This field works with the discount percent field in ICSP and PDSC. Keep in mind that this is the CASH discount, not the line or product discount. Content:

properties.Label: Terms Discount %
properties.Description: This field works in conjunction with the discount flag in ICSP and PDSC. It represents the cash discount, if any, to be used when this product is sold. This field comes in to play ONLY if the discount override flag is set to YES. This field normally serves only as a default to creating PDSC records. It is used directly only in OE and only when this product is sold without involving a PDSC record and then only if the discount override is YES. Zero is a valid entry if the override flag is YES and no discount is desired. Keep in mind that this is CASH discount, not product or line discount.

properties.Label: Last Change Time
properties.Description: This is the time portion of the last date/time a given record was changed. Record changed is defined by either an operator pressing GO from a setup screen, or the completion of a processing transaction (ie. Invoiced OE line) in batch type functions.

properties.Label: Counting Units
properties.Description: The counting unit represents the unit of measure to be used for cycle and physical count processes. As such, this field is used only in the ICEP* functions. The field is validated, if entered, from ICESU and SASTT. If not entered, all ICEP* functions will default to the stocking unit. Content:

properties.Label: Unit Conversions
properties.Description: This flag is set automatically, the user has no access to it. It is set to 'yes' by the creation of an ICSEU record for this product. It is set to 'no' by the deletion of the last ICSEU record for this product. The flag is used in the 'p-unit.i' object to speed the validation of entered units.

properties.Label: Selling Units
properties.Description: The selling unit is used as a default for all order entry processes. If entered, it is validated against ICSEU and SASTT entries. If left blank, all selling processes will default to the stocking unit. Note that this is used only as a default, not a mandatory selling unit.

properties.Label: Stocking Units
properties.Description: The stocking unit is required for every product. It is not validated against any unit setups and is always assumed to represent a single unit in all quantity fields for the product. It is normally 'each'. It is HIGHLY RECOMMENDED that the stocking unit be the smallest possible selling unit to avoid fractional quantities. The stocking unit is also used as an automatic default for all other units for the product. Any unit (other than stocking) that is left blank will be considered equal to the stocking unit. The stocking unit is the basis for all quantity transactions in Trend. As such, it is very important to not change the value of this field in mid-stream. Careful consideration must be given to the effect on: 1) Quantities and Balances in ICSW 2) Pricing in ICSW, PDS* 3) Outstanding orders, transfers, purchase orders 4) GL Balances 5) History on file

It is a four-level hierarchy coded as an eight-digit number, with an optional fifth level adding two more digits. Version 16, released in 2014,[1] contained over 50,000 commodities. Content:

In ICSL, minimum and target information can be expressed in weight. If so, all buying decisions will be compared to target weight, discounts will be expressed in weights met, and review cycle information (APSP) will be stored as total weight.

properties.Label: Last Invoiced Date
properties.Description: Last Invoice Date. This gets loaded in OEEPI. If an active reservation is found for the item during order entry, the system will store off that reservation on the oeelextra.custreserverowpointer field. Even if the line uses other reservations to fill the line quantity - pulling stock, the system will store the original active reservation. That is the reservation that the stock is sold against.

properties.Label: Expected Quantity
properties.Description: Total Quantity Expected. The amount that must be bought by the Customer/Ship To on the reservation to meet contractual agreement. Compared to Total Qty Sold to see if they met the requirements.

properties.Label: Required Quantity
properties.Description: Required Quantity. The quantity required to be available at anytime to meet the contractual reservation agreement for the customer/shipto. It may or may not be the same as the qtyexpected. Can be a longer contract so the expected total is higher for overall, but the required qty is a portion of the total. 10,000 total, but need 2500 on reserve at any given time.

properties.Label: Reserved Quantity
properties.Description: Reserved Quantity. - Amount of quantity pulled from ICSW based on quantity available at the time the Reservation is activated for this item. - Do not want to always replenish the full qty required each time, just what is needed based on current availability. - To Top Off the item via replenishment the system will take the qtyrequired less the qtyreserved on the ICSPCD record if set to replenish - This is the amount that the ICSW Reserved Qty is increased by, so no one else can take this reservation quantity. Content:

properties.Label: Sold Quantity
properties.Description: Total Quanty Sold. This gets loaded in OEEPI. If an active reservation is found for the item during order entry, the system will store off that reservation on the oeelextra.custreserverowpointer field. Even if the line uses other reservations to fill the line quantity - pulling stock, the system will store the original active reservation. That is the reservation that the stock is sold against. Used to compare to Total Quantity Expected for the contract to see if the Customer/Ship To meet the requirements for the number of items bought.

properties.Label: Replenish Stock
properties.Description: Does the reservation need to be replenished or not. One time reserved quantity or not. Content:

properties.Label: Certificate/License Required
properties.Description: For this Allowed Restriction, does it require a valid certification/license to continue with the sale of the product. In the ICSPR setup, if a certification is required, it does not require that a specific (ICSPR - type = "CL") exist in the setup. If there is a specific CL type record attched to the restriction, then there must be an active ICSPRC record found that matches to the Restriction Code and Customer/ ShipTo. If there are no CL type records attached to the ICSPR record, then as long as the system can find any cert/license for the current Restriction Code and Customer/Ship To (CSPRC record), then it will allow the sale of the product. Content:

properties.Description: Company Number - required

properties.Label: Created Date
properties.Description: The date the restrciton is created. They can maintain a restriction over time, but the initial created date will not change.

properties.Label: Expire Date
properties.Description: The system will only look for Restrictions within the start date, expire date range based on the order's request ship date, but the restriction has to active asl well.

properties.Label: Record Type
properties.Description: Used to identify the type of restriction record. The original restriction type is a Sales type restriction, but there is mention of other types that could make it in and want to use the same restriction table. S - Sales Restriction (only value used at this time) P - Purchase Restriction (future) T - Transfer Restriction (future) SRC - Sourcing (future) F - Freight Altitude (future) Content:

properties.Label: Restriction Code

properties.Label: Restriction Override
properties.Description: Can this restriction be overriden. Currently, this is limited to the OE Sales order, but may expand to other document types based on the Record Type of the record. If they answer 'yes' to this field, it states with proper Authorization in OE, the operator can force the use of an existing restriction and by pass the restriction. If this flag is not set, and this restrction is found, the Restriction Override field in OE will not even be enterable. Content:

properties.Label: Restriction Type
properties.Description: The ICSPR record is created for Product Type restrictions. PR-Product Restriction (can be Product - ICSP or Catalog - ICSC) BC-Brand Code PL-Product Line PC-Product Category PT-Product Price Type AG-Alternate Prod Cat (future) Content:

properties.Label: Row Pointer
properties.Description: This is the Row Pointer of the Restriction record and is used in the icsprt.srcrowpointer field (child of the ICSPR record). We use the row pointer since the parent record could be prod, catelog, prod cat, vendno. prodline, brand code, alt prod group, etc and no need to duplicate all those fields within the child table. properties.Label: Price/Cost Units Per Stk Unit
properties.Description: Represents the special pricing/cost unit conversion. In particular, the number of pricing units per stocking unit. This field is used only if using the special pricing/costing unit conversion (see speccostty). Note that this field cannot be negative, but will often be less than one. Note also the direction of conversion - number of special units in a stocking unit. Examples: Item Priced by Hundred - csunperstk = .01 unitstock = "EACH" Item Priced by Board Foot - csunperstk = 3.5 unitstock = "EACH" (meaning this board is equal to 3.5 boardfoot) This conversion factor will be used for all pricing. In the first example, a price of $10 would equal .10/EACH (10 * .01 * Qty). In the second example, a price of $10 would equal $35/EACH (10 * 3.5 * Qty).

properties.Label: ABC Customer Class
properties.Description: Dr. Barry Lawrence of Texas A&M University has created a new inventory classification method called the ABC classification of inventory. The classification is determined by Gross Margin Return on Investment (GMROI), Dollar Sales Volume, Unit Sales Volume and Customer Criticality. This field stores the ranking for the customer criticality of a product. The ranking is determined by the branch manager; it is notcalculated. It takes into account the significance of the product to the customer and the significance of the customer to the distributor. The customer criticality ranking will take precedence over all other ABC classification rankings when determining the final ABC classification. Content:

properties.Label: ABC Final Class
properties.Description: Dr. Barry Lawrence of Texas A&M University has created a new inventory classification method called the ABC classification of inventory. The classification is determined by Gross Margin Return on Investment (GMROI), Dollar Sales Volume, Unit Sales Volume and Customer Criticality. This field stores the final ABC classification of the product in this warehouse. The GMROI, Dollar Sales and Unit Sales are weighted then combined to determine the final classification. If a customer criticality ranking has been entered, it takes precedence over the value calculated. Content:

properties.Label: ABC GMROI Class
properties.Description: Dr. Barry Lawrence of Texas A&M University has created a new inventory classification method called the ABC classification of inventory. The classification is determined by Gross Margin Return on Investment (GMROI), Dollar Sales Volume, Unit Sales Volume and Customer Criticality. This field stores the ranking for Gross Margin Return on Investment (GMROI) of a product. The GMROI is calculated by dividing the gross margin for a product by the average inventory cost of that product. The ranking is determined based on the GMROI value. Content:

properties.Label: Over Expiration

The classification is determined by Gross Margin Return on Investment (GMROI), Dollar Sales Volume, Unit Sales Volume and Customer Criticality. This field stores the ranking for the customer criticality of a product. The ranking is determined by the branch manager; it is not calculated. It takes into account the significance of the product to the customer and the significance of the customer to the distributor. The customer criticality ranking will take precedence over all other ABC classification rankings when determining the final ABC classification. properties.Description: Authorized Replenishment Path Push Flag. This flag is used only if the the ARP is from another location, not if from vendor. A true value indicates that the supplying location will push product to the the receiving location (this branch). A false indicates that the receiving location (this location) will request product when needed from the supplying branch. Note that this flag defaults from ICSL if vendor/line is provided, then from ICSD.

properties.Label: Authorized Replenishment Path
properties.Description: Indicates the source for replenishing this product in this location. This field defaults first from ICSL (if vendor/line is provided) then from ICSD. Content:

properties.Label: arpusage
properties.Description: "This field is a pv-delimited field that stores warehouse and usage rate for all baby branches at the mother branch only. The data is accessible from a button in ICIP under the replenishment tab and will provide the user with the numbers that determined their usage rate IF they have turned on ""A""verage usage in the new ICSR setting. This was rename of field xxc1 used in 3.1."

properties.Label: ARP Vendor #
properties.Description: The vendor from which this item is normally purchased. In the case of a product with several vendors this should be the primary vendor. The vendor number is required only if the arptype is 'v', but it should always be provided. Many of the IC reports and inquiries include vendor ranges or options that will work properly only if the vendor is provided regardless of the ARP. This field is validated against APSV.

properties.Label: ARP Whse
properties.Description: This field is used only if the arptype is 'w'. The field can be filled in regardless of arptype but will be used by Trend only with the 'w' arptype. It indicates the source branch for replenishment for this product in this branch.

properties.Label: ASQ $ Diff
properties.Help: Maximum Dollar Difference Allowed to Increase Order Point By

properties.Label: AutoeSrcBO
properties.Help: If yes, Automatically Sends BO's to eSource on Request

properties.Label: Auto BO Fill
properties.Help: Fill Back Orders Automatically (Not Used in Full Order Fill)
properties.Description: This field is used to control back order fill for this product. If 'true', this product will be considered during all back order fill processing. If no, this product will not be included in the process and the entire quantity received will be released for manual fill.

properties.Label: Stock Available
properties.Description: This date indicates the date that stock became available after a stock out situation. This date is maintained automatically by all receiving processes. If there is no stock available at the time that product was received, then the product is considered to be stock out and the stock out available date is set to today. This works in conjunction with the last stock out date and the number of days stock out to make extended stock out decisions for ICAM. The number of days stock out is also set by the receiving process.

properties.Label: Average
properties.Description: Average Cost. This field is maintained by the system and should not be changed by the user. It is protected by the see cost flag in SASOO. This field is an integral part of IC balancing. The average cost represents the average cost of the items in stock. It is updated by all process affecting inventory quantities. This field is stored either in stocking units or in 'raw' cost - special price/cost units. Average cost is updated during receiving by taking the old cost times the old qty, adding the received quantity times the new cost, and dividing the sum by the new total quantity: $10 * 50 = 500 $15 * 10 = 150 == === 60 650 $650 / 60 = 10.833 each A similar process is done if items are removed from stock at any cost other than average. IC Balancing documents explain the entire process.

properties.Label: Avg LT Date
properties.Description: The average lead time date represents the last time that an average lead time was calculated. This is set by any procedure that calculates lead time. Generally, this is any receiving process.

properties.Label: Base Price
properties.Description: The base price is a customer price for this product in this location. It is commonly used as a multiplier for PDSC records. As such, it can represent a particular column price, the lowest acceptable price, or the published price. This field can be updated manually or by a number of PD functions, inlcuding automatic update tapes. Base price is used by all pricing programs, including order entry. Base Price is always in stocking units unless the product has special price/cost units, in which case it is in the special price unit.

properties.Label: LIFO Base Year Cost
properties.Description: This represents the LIFO cost for this product. Like all costs, it is in stocking units unless special price/costing is used for this product. This cost cannot be used for any updating process but is available on several IC reports, including a comparitive trial balance. The cost is calculated by the system using ICROV. The option exists to run this report in updating mode. If that is done this cost will be updated.

properties.Label: Bill on Receipt
properties.Description: A product can be set up as Bill on Receipt in a storeroom managed warehouse. These products are replenished and sold from a storeroom managed warehouse but are not usually stocked as distributor owned inventory. Instead, when these products are received through a Purchase Order or Warehouse Transfer, they are automatically "sold" to the warehouse (customer). This will then move the inventory to customer owned.

properties.Label: Bin Loc #1
properties.Description: First bin location for this product. Bin locations are in the format BB/RR/SSS/FFF B-Building R-Row S-Section F-Shelf Bin locations are not required but are heavily used by all physical and cycle count operations. Implementing physical counts without bin locations will be difficult. Implementing cycle counts without bin locations is impossible. Every product should be assigned to a unique bin location for a given warehouse. The system does not ensure uniqueness. Bin location 1 is considered the primary location where bin location 2, if present, is the overflow or secondary location. If the product is warehouse manager controlled the bin locations in ICSW will not be used.

properties.Label: Bin Loc #2
properties.Description: See binloc1.

properties.Label: Bin Type
properties.Help: Whse Mgr - Bin Type Restriction, Blank for No Restriction
properties.Description: Bin Type is used only if this product in this location is warehouse manager controlled. It indicates the type of bin used to store this product. This is used by the automatic put-away system to ensure that a product does not get assigned to the wrong kind of bin. This field, if entered, is validated against WMST. If the bin type is left blank it indicates that this product has no bin restrictions.

properties.Label: BO All if Short
properties.Help: If Net Available Doesn't Cover Qty Order, BO All of Qty Order
properties.Description: This flag controls back orders in order entry. If true it indicates that partial line fills are not allowed on this product - if any quantity is not available the entire quantity must be back ordered.

properties.Label: Product Class
properties.Description: The class field can be maintained by the user or can be set by the inventory classification system (ICAI). The system uses the Gordon Graham 1 - 13 classification system as oppossed to the more traditional A/B/C method. Content:

properties.Label: Frozen
properties.Help: (Y)es to Prevent Product Class From Being Recalculated
properties.Description: Indicates that the user has chosen to lock in the classification of this product (see 'class'). This product is then skipped in the classification process.

properties.Label: Company #
properties.Description: Identifies the Company under which the record was created.

properties.Label: Count Required
properties.Description: Count Flag. If set to 'true', it indicates that this product should be counted during the next physical or cycle count (ICEPP or ICEPC). This flag can be set to true by the user. Certain functions in Trend (OEES for example) allow the user to set the flag based on feedback information. Other processes (OEEPI for example) will set the flag automatically based on odd stock situations. Products with the countfl set to true will automatically appear on the next count in addition to the products that would appear due to range or option settings.

properties.Label: Country of Origin
properties.Description: The country in which a product was manufactured, produced, or grown. Used as part of the hierachy to load the HS tariff code on an OE line or PO line for both a stocked product and a nonstock product. Content:

properties.Label: Critical Product
properties.Description: When a product is flagged as a critical product, that indicates that it is important that the product have stock on hand in the storeroom managed warehouse. Cycle counting can be done specifically for products set up as critical products.

properties.Label: Cust Average
properties.Description: Average Cost of customer owned inventory in a storeroom managed warehouse. This field is maintained by the system and should not be changed by the user. It is protected by the see cost flag in SASOO. This field is an integral part of IC balancing. The average cost represents the average cost of the items in stock. It is updated by all process affecting inventory quantities. This field is stored either in stocking units or in 'raw' cost - special price/cost units. Average cost is updated during receiving by taking the old cost times the old qty, adding the received quantity times the new cost, and dividing the sum by the new total quantity: $10 * 50 = 500 $15 * 10 = 150 == === 60 650 $650 / 60 = 10.833 each A similar process is done if items are removed from stock at any cost other than average.

properties.Label: Cust Fixed
properties.Description: Fixed Cost of customer owned inventory in a storeroom managed warehouse.

properties.Label: Cust Last
properties.Description: Last Cost of customer owned inventory in a storeroom managed warehouse.

properties.Label: Customer Owned
properties.Description: This flag is used to indicate if all inventory for a product set up in a storeroom managed warehouse is owned by the customer and that the customer is responsible for the purchasing of the product to restock the storeroom.

properties.Label: Cust On Hand
properties.Description: This field stores the amount of a product currently on hand that is owned by the customer in a storeroom managed warehouse.

properties.Label: Cust On Order
properties.Description: This field stores the amount of a product currently on order that is owned by the customer in a storeroom managed warehouse.

properties.Label: Cust Received
properties.Description: This field stores the amount of a product currently received that is owned by the customer in a storeroom managed warehouse. Anyplace customer owned stock can be received into the system as a receipt, it will load the CISW value. The value is used in BO Fill to determine the amount of the receipt that is customer owned versus distributor owned. Currently, the only place this is loaded is from WTEI.

properties.Label: Cust Unavailable
properties.Description: This field stores the amount of a product currently marked as unavailable inventory that is owned by the customer in a storeroom managed warehouse.

properties.Label: DATC
properties.Description: The DATC cost can be used for any type of line-level addon costs. It follows the rules and visibility of all other costs. It is commonly used either for Destination Area Transportation Charges or Rush Purchasing charges. This amount is used, if present, in order entry. A series or AO options in IC and OE control the method of application.

properties.Label: Status Change 852
properties.Help: Used for POEVP 852 ION BOD Interface

properties.Label: Entered
properties.Description: The date when the ICSW record was first entered.

This flag is used only by the expedite report (PORBX). It is a temporary setting to record that this product has already been reported for this reason. This reason indicates a zero availability with existing backorders.

properties.Label: Available < Safety Allowance
properties.Description: Used only by the expedite report (PORBX). This flag is set by the report to indicate that this product has already appeared on the report once. This flag indicates a net available less than the safety stock level Content:

properties.Label: Stock Level 0 for 30 Days
properties.Description: This field is used by the expedite report. It is temporarily set to indicate those items that have already appeared on the report for this reason. This flag is used for extended stock out reporting.

properties.Label: Family Group
properties.Description: The family group type is a grouping method used on RRAR to indicate items that should be ordered together. This goes beyond the vendor and line to specific items groups. For example, you might want to set drills and drill bits in the same family groups. This field is used only for RRAR. If entered, it is validated by SASTT type I.

properties.Label: Frozen By
properties.Description: This is a logical field that indicates whether the ordering controls were set by the computer or by the end user. The flag is set automatically based on ICAM or the user freezing the product. Content:

properties.Label: Freeze LT
properties.Help: (0) Don't Freeze, (999) Freeze or (###) Days To Keep LT Above

properties.Label: Frozen Date
properties.Description: Indicates the month and year that this product was last frozen. This is used for user information and by the ICAM product in conjunction with the 'frozenmos' field to determine when the product should come off the frozen list and be brought back into the ICAM calculation loop.

properties.Label: Frozen Months
properties.Help: Warning: Frozen Months Should Not be Changed (8632)
properties.Description: Indicates the number of months frozen. This field can be set by either the user or the computer (through ICAM). This field is used by ICAM to determine when the product should be 'unfrozen' and brought back into the ICAM calculation loop. If set to '99' (the system will never set to this) the product will be considered frozen forever.

properties.Label: Frozen Reason
properties.Description: The frozen type corresponds to table entries in SASTT, Type 'F'. This field will be used by the system whenever ICAM freezes a product and should be used by the user for the same purposes.

properties.Label: G.S.T. Status
properties.Description: GST is the Canadian Goods and Services Tax. The status field is used to indicate that the item is taxable or exempt. True equals taxable. This field appears on screen and is used only if the company country code is set to 'CA'. Content:

properties.Label: Hi-5 $ Diff
properties.Help: Maximum Dollar Difference Allowed to Increase Order Point By

properties.Label: Incl Unavail Reason Qty
properties.Description: Used primarily from StoreRoom to flag an item for Unavailable inspection during the receiving process. So stock gets set asside as unavailable for inspection, but this field setting of 'P' allows for the PO replenishment to include Unavailable Qty in the available stock totals so they do not order too much stock when there really is stock available. If the Unavailable Reason is flagged for StoreRoom inspection, then the unavailable qty with that reason is included in the Qty Available during Replenishment (via ICSOU Totals and reasons). Content:

properties.Label: YTD - Issues
properties.Description: Units issued year to date. This field is always stored in stocking units. It is accumulative, cleared only by year end processing (ICAY)

properties.Label: Word Index
properties.Description: Internal field used for keyword processing Content:

properties.Label: Regrind Labor Product
properties.Description: If a product has been defined as a regrind product, that product, when consumed, is able to be reground, sharpened, repaired or refurbished into a usable product. A labor product can be associated with a regrind product which will be used as part of the regrind process. Content:

properties.Label: Last 852 Avail
properties.Help: Updated During EDI 852 with Purchasing Net Available

properties.Label: Cycle Cnt
properties.Description: This field indicates that last time this product was counted using either physical or cycle counting. It is updated automatically through ICEPP and ICEPC. If the count is cancelled it is reset. It is possible to run physical counts by picking up only those products not counted since a certain date. This field is used for that report criteria.

properties.Label: Last
properties.Description: This field follows the standard cost storage and viewing criteria. It is updated when product is received from the ARP for the product. Last cost can be used for SM/GL updating but it is a very poor way to interface to GL. Last cost can also be used as the default cost on all PO's.

properties.Label: Last Foreign Cost
properties.Description: Last Foreign Cost. This cost also follows the unit and viewing rules of all costs, but this cost is stored in the currency of the ARP vendor for the product. It is used only when the currency (on APSV) is not blank. When cutting PO's for a foreign vendor, either the last foreign cost or the foreign replacement cost will be used as the default for the line item price depending upon how the AO - Documents - Purchase Orders - Entry Defaults: Foreign Cost field is set.

properties.Label: Invoice
properties.Description: Indicates that last date that this item appeared on an invoice. This is updated by OEEPI only.

properties.Label: Last LT Date
properties.Description: Indicates the date of the last lead time for this product. This date is used by PO and WT receiving to determine if a new average can be calculated. The field is then updated to current by these functions.

properties.Label: PO or WT
properties.Description: Last PO or WT date. Indicates the date of the last document requesting inventory for this item. This field is updated whenever a PO or WT is cut.

properties.Label: Receipt
properties.Description: Indicates the last time this product was received, either through PO or WT (POEI/WTEI). It is not updated from IC functions.

properties.Label: Last Stock Out
properties.Description: Indicates the last time this item when stock out. This is set automatically by OEEPI and WTES whenever the quantity on hand goes to zero.

properties.Label: Avg Lead Time
properties.Description: The average lead time for this product in days. This is calculated automatically by any receiving function. The average is calculated across the current receipt, the last receipt, and the previous receipt. If a lead time is more than six months old the average is not calculated.

properties.Label: Last Lead Time
properties.Description: Last lead time. After calculating a new average, this field is set based on the lead time of the current receipt. This is updated by all receiving functions (POEI and WTEI).

properties.Label: Prior Lead Time
properties.Description: Lead Time Prior. The last lead time is moved to this field prior to setting a new last lead time but after calculating a new average lead time. This occurs in POEI and WTEI.

properties.Label: Line Point/Max
properties.Description: Line Point for ordering controls. For most ordering types, the line point is the point where RRAR will pick up this item for reordering providing the line is already in a review state. This field is set by ICAM using standard Gordon Graham methods. If the ordering type is min/max, this field is used to store the maximum stock point.

properties.Label: Linked Regrind Product
properties.Description: If a product is not set up as a regrind product, this product can be linked to a regrind product indicating that it is used as part of the regrind process. If a product has been defined as a regrind product, that product, when consumed, is able to be reground, sharpened, repaired or refurbished into a usable product.

properties.Label: List Price
properties.Description: List Price. Customer List or Retail Price. This field is based either on stocking units or special pricing unit. See base price for a complete explanation.

properties.Label: Review Days
properties.Help: # of Days Ahead of Season to Review Product for Purchase
properties.Description: Number of seasonal review days. This indicates the number of days prior to season begin for preseason buying. It is used by the seasonal analysis report (ICRIP) to bring the product to the buyer's attention at the appropriate time to conduct pre-season buys. It is user input and maintained.

properties.Label: # Days Stockout
properties.Help: Warning: Stock Out Information Should Not be Changed (8633)
properties.Description: In days, the length of the last stock out for this product. This information is maintained by the system in conjunction with the last stock out date and the stock available date. These are set by the various functions that relieve and receive goods.

properties.Label: Non-Discountable Product
properties.Description: Used to identify a product that cannot be discounted. This field is used in the Promote/Equate integration to determine if an item is eligible for discounts.

properties.Label: OAN - Non Stock
properties.Description: Used to identify a product as being created from Non Stock. This field is used in conjunction with icsw.statustype. When the statustype is set to 'o' for Order As Needed then this field may contain a blank value (to indicate a regular OAN product) or an 'n' (to indicate an OAN-NS product). When the statustype field is changed from 'o' to any other value, this field must be cleared. Content:

properties.Label: Non Tax Reason
properties.Description: This field is used to store a type code for a non-taxable item, indicating why the product is exempt from sales tax in this location. Any entry is validated against SASTT type N. If the item is nontaxable this is a required field. It is used by the tax analysis report (SMRT) to group like items.

properties.Label: No Promotions Allowed
properties.Description: Used to determine if promotions are allowed for a product. This field is used in the Promote/Equate integration to determine if promotional pricing is applicable for an item.

properties.Label: # Stockouts
properties.Help: Warning: Stock Out Information Should Not be Changed (8633)
properties.Description: Indicates the number of times this item has been in a stock out condition. This field is set automatically by the system but is never reset by the system.

properties.Label: Raw Line Pt
properties.Help: Month End Merge Calculated Line Point Prior to Adjusters

properties.Label: Raw Order Point
properties.Help: Month End Merge Calculated Order Point Prior to Adjusters

properties.Label: Last Change By
properties.Description: Tags the record with the login initials of the last operator to update the record. Last update is defined by the operator pressing GO on a setup screen, or by the completion of a transaction in a batch updating process.

properties.Label: Order Method
properties.Help: E)OQ, C)lass, M)in/Max, Q)tyBrk, B)lanket, H)uman
properties.Description: The order calculate type determines the method to be used in calculating the quantity to order when this product needs to be ordered. It is used by ICAM to determine and set the order quantity. Note that it is not used by RRAR except in the case of Min/Max. Order quantities are calculated dynamically for Min/Max. This field also appears on a large number of IC and PO reports. Content:

properties.Label: Order Point/Min
properties.Description: Order Point. This is the basic quantity used by RRAR functions to determine when to order product. It is calculated by ICAM and includes safety stock. The calculation is usage during the ordering period (determined by lead time) plus safety stock. For example: 30 used per month 10 days lead time 50% safety stock Used during lead time = 10 (one per day for ten days lead time) Safety Stock = 5 (50% of usage during lead time or 10) Order Point = 15

properties.Label: Order Qty
properties.Description: Order Quantity. This is the quantity that RRAR will use when ordering this product. If will be used for all types except Min/Max. If the item is seasonal this field is the in season quantity. If the item is not seasonal this is the only quantity used.

properties.Label: Product Line
properties.Description: product line. this value must be defined in the ICSL table

properties.Label: Product Preference
properties.Description: This field is optional. The product preference is set up in SASTT and validated in ICSW. Product preferences are used to group products and refer to priority to to manage SKU's. Product tiers refer to quality and are assigned in ICSP. Exceptions can be set up in ICSEE. Content:

properties.Label: Backorder
properties.Description: Qty backordered on the OE line items

properties.Label: Committed
properties.Description: The committed quantity is a result of the product being picked from the warehouse. When an order is initially placed in Order Entry the quantity is placed in the Reserved field. When the pick tickets are printed, the Reserved quantity is decreased and the Committed quantity is increased. The Committed quantity is decreased when the order is invoiced through OE Entry Processing Invoice Processing.

properties.Label: Demand
properties.Help: Warehouse Transfer, Kit Production, Value Add Demand

properties.Label: WT In Transit
properties.Description: This is the qty in transit from one warehouse to another

properties.Label: On Hand
properties.Description: Qty on hand . This field plus qtyrcvd and qtyunavail are used to calculate the current inventory value.

properties.Label: Received
properties.Description: Qty Received. this field plus qtyonhand and qtyunavail are used to calculate the current inventory.

properties.Label: Reserved
properties.Description: The Reserved quantity is the quantity currently reserved for sale to customers or transferred to warehouses. This does not include the quantities that have already been picked and staged for the customer. (Those quantities go into Committed.) This quantity is increased by orders entered in Order Entry or approved transfers in Warehouse Transfer. The quantity is decreased when the product is picked through OE Entry Processing Pick Tickets and WT Entry Print Warehouse Transfer.

properties.Label: Unavailable
properties.Description: Qty Unavailable. this field plus qtyrcvd and qtyunavail are used to calculate the current inventory.

properties.Label: Freeze Ranks
properties.Help: Freeze the Warehouse and Company Ranks

properties.Label: Rcv as Unavail
properties.Description: This field controls whether product receipts will automatically go into unavailable inventory.

properties.Label: Rebate Sub Type
properties.Help: Product Rebate Sub Type for Grouping

properties.Label: Regrind Flag
properties.Description: This field indicates if the product, when consumed, is able to be reground, sharpened, repaired or refurbished into a usable product Content:

properties.Label: Replacement
properties.Description: replacement cost

properties.Label: Repl Cost Dt
properties.Help: Date the Replacement Cost was Last Changed
properties.Description: The date that the replacement cost was last changed

properties.Label: Replacement Foreign Cost
properties.Description: Foreign Replacement Cost. This cost also follows the unit and viewing rules of all costs, but this cost is stored in the currency of the ARP vendor for the product. It is used only when the currency (on APSV) is not blank. When cutting PO's for a foreign vendor, either the last foreign cost or the foreign replacement cost will be used as the default for the line item price depending upon how the AO - Documents - Purchase Orders - Entry Defaults: Foreign Cost field is set.

properties.Label: Reservation Type
properties.Description: This field changes the timing at which inventory is actually reserved for an order. The reservation type can be assigned as (d)elayed, against (r)eceipts, (a)lways reserve, or be left blank. Each type defines a different level of hierarchical rules that dictate when and if the product will be reserved upon entry. Content:

properties.Label: Row Pointer
properties.Description: A unique identifier that can be used to link other records to this particular record. Content:

properties.Label: 852 Out
properties.Help: Updated During EDI 852 With Current Date
properties.Description: This field will indicate that last time this product/warehouse was reported on the EDI 852 document. If it blank, it has never been reported. It will be updated at the end of the 852 processing, but is output to the 852 flat file prior to the updating. This will allow the Vendor to know that if the field is blank, this is the first time the product has been reported. While this field is enterable in ICSWB, it should not be manipulated except in certain situations. Once such situation would be that the customer is converting to TREND and was using the 852 on their prior system, then they would want to update this date either with the conversion process or manually to show that this product was previously transmitted on an EDI 852.

properties.Label: Safety Allowance
properties.Description: Stores the safety allowance amount in stocking units. When the icsw.safeallty = "Q", this field will be updated directly from the screen. When the icsw.safeallty = "%", this field will be calculated based on the icsw.safeallpct field. Content:

properties.Label: Safety Allowance
properties.Description: Stores safety allowance as a percent When the icsw.safeallty = "%", this field is directly updated from the screen. When the icsw.safeallty = "Q", this field will be calculated from the icsw.safeallamt field. Content:

properties.Label: Safety Type
properties.Description: This field works in conjunction with icsw.safeallamt and icsw.safeallpct. If icsw.safeallty is ("Q"), then the icsw.safeallamt is updateable in the ICSW function and the icsw.safeallpct is calculated. If icsw.safeallty is ("%"), then the icsw.safeallpct is updateable in the ICSW function and the icsw.safeallamt is calculated from the percent value. Content:

properties.Label: SafetyFrzFl
properties.Description: This field is used to indicate the icsw(product level) safety data will be used and it will not allow overrides from the new ICSR settings.

properties.Label: Season Begin
properties.Description: The month (2-digit numeric) that the season for this product begins.

properties.Label: Season End
properties.Description: The month (2-digit numeric) that the season for this product ends.

properties.Label: SeasonFrzFl
properties.Description: This field is used to indicate the icsw(product level) seasonal data will be used and it will not allow overrides from the new ICSR settings.

properties.Label: Extended Type
properties.Description: Identifies whether the product is a serial product, a lot product, or neither Content:

properties.Label: Shelf Life Product
properties.Description: When a product is flagged as a shelf life product in a storeroom mananged warehouse, that indicates that the product can only be stocked for a limited amount of time before the product is no longer usable. Cycle counting can be done specifically for products set up as shelf life products.

properties.Label: SL Update Date
properties.Help: Date Last Updated Through Supplier Link

properties.Label: Sales Manager

properties.Label: Serial Receiving
properties.Description: This field determines when the serial number is to be assigned Content:

properties.Label: Machine

properties.Description: Status type. This field is used in conjunction with icsw.nonstockty. properties.Label: Surplus Type

properties.Label: HS Code
properties.Description: Harmonized System Tariff Code. The HS system uses a logical nomenclature method to categorize goods into approximately 5,000 commodity groups. Countries often assign customs duties based on the harmonized tariff code of the product. Used as part of the hierachy to load the HS tariff code on an OE line or PO line for both a stocked product and a nonstock product. Content:

properties.Label: Last Trans
properties.Description: Records the date when a given record was last changed. Last changed is defined by an operator pressing GO from a setup screen, or the completion of a batch processing transaction.

properties.Label: Trans Proc

properties.Label: Field Name
properties.Description: The name of the database field on the record specified in the RECORDTY field which can hold the name of an individual. If the individulal is placed on a GDPR restriction, this field will be used to indicate to the UI that it may need to be hidden to prevent the propagation of the name. Content:

properties.Label: GDPR Type
properties.Description: A single character code that indicates if the field specified by FIELDNM and any associated personal data are on GDPR restriction. If the margin amount or margin percentage on the Order Entry order is less than the SASO minumum margin amount or SASO minimum margin percentage respectively, the OE order will be placed on hold and the character loaded in this field will appear in the Approval Type field on the OE header. Also, if the margin amount or margin percentage on the OE order is more than the SASO maximum margin amount or SASO maximum margin percentage respectively, the OE order will be placed on hold and the character loaded in this field will appear in the Approval Type field on the OE header. properties.Label: Actual Freight Amount
properties.Help: Amount of freight based on carrier charges, w/o billing add-ons
properties.Description: The actual freight on this suffix of the order. This field is updated only from PM and is not enterable in Trend.

properties.Label: Addon Amt
properties.Description: This arrayed field has 4 occurances: 1 - freight in (or addon 1) 2 - freight out (or addon 2) 3 - addon 3 4 - addon 4 The addons default onto the order from the ARSCO addon defaults (the addons are setup and described in SASTO). They are overrideable. The second addon, freight, will be updated from PM if not overridden in OE. The addon amount reflects the dollar or percentage addon (based on the addon type of a $ or %). It does not take into account the minimum or zero addon value. The calculated addon, considering these factors, is stored in addonnet. As of SX 4.0, the addons are found in the addon table

properties.Label: Net Addon Amount
properties.Description: Contains the calculated addon figure. It is calculated from the addon amount ($ or %) and takes into account the zero level or minimum addon charge defined in SASTO. As of SX 4.0, the addons are found in the addon table

properties.Label: Addons
properties.Description: The addon number is required for each addon amount entered. The addon number correlates to the addon defined in SASTO. It is defaulted from the customer record when the order is entered, but can be overridden. As of SX 4.0, the addons are found in the addon table Content:
This field describes how the addon is calculated - as a percentage or dollar value. As of SX 4.0, the addons are found in the addon table Content:

properties.Label: Addon Override
properties.Description: Indicates if the addon has been overridden. If the addon is manually typed in on the addon screen, this flag will be set to yes. Content:

properties.Label: Address Override
properties.Description: Used in conjuction with AvaTax Address Verification and may be enhanced to include other address verifications. Yes indicates that the address verification failed but the entered address should be saved as is (perhaps it is a new address not yet in the USPS database). For AvaTax, yes will automatically replace address 2 with "General Delivery" when taxes are calculated.

properties.Label: Tax Group
properties.Description: This is the tax group identified with the addon. Each addon can be taxed or not taxed, and can be taxed relative to specific tax percentages defined in SASGS and SASGL by tax group. The tax group determines which tax percentages apply to this particular addon. Content:

properties.Description: This field allows an order to be identified as a Bill on Receipt order. This field will default to ?no? and will be automatically set to ?yes? when an order is created from the Bill on Receipt process. This field will also be available for manual entry on the OEET Header tab if the warehouse is a Storeroom managed warehouse. Otherwise, it will be hidden.

properties.Label: BO Exists
properties.Description: Indicates if a back order was created and currently exists on this suffix.

properties.Label: B/O
properties.Description: Indicates if the customer accepts back orders. It default from the customer.

properties.Label: BO's Need Totalling
properties.Description: Indicates if a back order needs to be created or adjusted. (As of 3.1, this field is no longer used)

properties.Label: BO
properties.Description: If this field is yes, the suffix is a back order. If no, it is not a back order. This is particularly pertinent on a JIT order or a BR where the suffix number will not determine if a suffix is a back order.

properties.Label: Back Order of Release #
properties.Description: If borelfl is yes (indicating this is a back order), borelno contains the release which was back ordered. This field is relevant for BR and JITS. For example: if 01 represents a blanket release, and 02 is a back order of 01, and 03 is a back order of 02, then the borelfl for both 02 and 03 will be 01. Even though 03 is a backorder from 02, the ORIGINAL release order is 01 and the borelfl will point to the ORIGINAL release.

properties.Label: BO Stage
properties.Description: The stage in which the order should be back ordered. It is loaded from the OEAOB screen when the order is entered. If the OEAOB option is changed, open orders are not changed. Content:

properties.Label: BP Quote #
properties.Description: This is the Bid Prep quote# if the order was created from the Bid Prep system. There should only be a value in this field if the order was created from Bid Prep. The bpquoteno will be passed into the OE Batch Order during the Bid Prep Release process, then passed into the OEEH record when the new sales order is created by OEEBU.

properties.Label: Cancel
properties.Description: The cancel date can be manually entered by an operator. If entered, it indicates that this order must be picked prior to the cancel date or the order will be cancelled. OEEPC or OEEPI will actually cancel the order. NOTE: the cancel date IS NOT set when an order is manually cancelled.

properties.Label: Cart Identifier

properties.Description: This is a new field assigned at the time of tendering in OEET. There are certain coditions that apply before the field is available (not an rm, not a back order, no other payments made, credit card installed). It will allow the operator to post the tendered amounts directly for settlement versus authoriztion.

properties.Label: COD Collected

properties.Label: COD

ICSD - Whse (icsd.cnconfirmshipfl) ARSC - Customer (arsc.cnconfirmshipty) When all the Packages are Shipped and either of the settings in ARSC or ICSD are set to confirm shipments, then the field value is set to 'yes' Content:

properties.Label: DATC
properties.Description: Indicates that the DATC cost (the label can be user defined on the OEAO screen) has been manually overridden on the addon screen. Once the DATC cost is manually overridden, it will no longer be maintained from line entry or maintenance. Content:

properties.Label: Dex Flag
properties.Description: Indicates that the order came in from Batch OE as an invoiced order. This flag was added so that the order would not be retotaled using current taxing rates or WO discounts, etc. The order will typically be transmitted from a remote site (and has already been invoiced in that remote site). Therefore, the value of the order can not be changed.

properties.Label: Disc Dt
properties.Description: The date up to which the discount can be taken when cash is received in ARECE. Content:

properties.Label: Division #
properties.Description: The division for the order. It is used for division GL postings when the order is invoiced. Content:

properties.Label: # Delivery Printed
properties.Description: # of Delivery Documents Printed

properties.Label: Delivery Print Type
properties.Description: Delivery Document Print Price Type. Will default from ARSC and will only be enterable if arsc.dlvprintty = "O". In this case, the user must select the delivery print type. Web Only Content:

properties.Label: Domestic Tax Amt 1
properties.Description: The state tax amount (US Company) or the PST tax amount (Canadian Company) in the domestic currency of the distributor. This field is only loaded when the taxes are calculated using Taxware. The tax amount in the currency of the customer is stored in oeeh.taxamt[1]. If you mulitiply the foreign currency value in oeeh.taxamt[1] by the exchange rate stored in oeeh.salesexrate, you will get the value stored in this field.

properties.Label: Domestic Tax Amt 2
properties.Description: The county tax amount (US Company) n the domestic currency of the distributor. This field is only loaded when the taxes are calculated using Taxware. The tax amount in the currency of the customer is stored in oeeh.taxamt[2]. If you mulitiply the foreign currency value in oeeh.taxamt[2] by the exchange rate stored in oeeh.salesexrate, you will get the value stored in this field.

properties.Label: Domestic Tax Amt 3
properties.Description: The local tax amount (US Company) n the domestic currency of the distributor. This field is only loaded when the taxes are calculated using Taxware. The tax amount in the currency of the customer is stored in oeeh.taxamt[3]. If you mulitiply the foreign currency value in oeeh.taxamt[3] by the exchange rate stored in oeeh.salesexrate, you will get the value stored in this field.

properties.Label: Domestic Tax Amt 4
properties.Description: The federal tax amount (US Company) or the GST tax amount (Canadian Company) in the domestic currency of the distributor. This field is only loaded when the taxes are calculated using Taxware. The tax amount in the currency of the customer is stored in oeeh.taxamt[4]. If you mulitiply the foreign currency value in oeeh.taxamt[4] by the exchange rate stored in oeeh.salesexrate, you will get the value stored in this field.

properties.Label: Downpayment
properties.Description: The actual down payment amount associated with this release/suffix. If a non-CS order is tendered, the down payment amount will reflect the amount that has been tendered. If an order is over tendered (based on the shipped amount), the operator will have the option to move part of the down payment amount to the back order. An order will not be invoiced if the down payment amount is greater than the order value. NOTE: The down payment amount and payment amounts must be in synch.

properties.Label: Down Payment Type
properties.Description: Indicates the type of down payment - in $ or a %. The down payment is always stored as a dollar amount, but can be entered as a percentage. Content:

properties.Label: Email Address
properties.Help: Email Address for the Customer Placing the Order

properties.Label: Entered
properties.Description: The date the order was entered. When a back order or release is created, the enter date is reset to the date the back order or release is created. Content:

properties.Label: Enter Time
properties.Description: The time the order was entered. When a back order or release is created, this time is reset to the time the back order or release is created. Content:

properties.Label: ESB Invoice Flag
properties.Description: Indicates the invoice information has been sent to the SOA Business Information Service

properties.Label: ESB Quote Flag
