properties.Description: This field will identify the special price/costing data that is related to this record. This number can be matched up to the ICSS record with the primary unique key k-icss.

properties.Label: Instructions
properties.Description: This field is used on a reference component to store the lengthy reference. It prints on document prints.

properties.Label: Lead Time
properties.Description: The time in days required to replenish the component product. This can be used to determine when the completed product will be available. Content:

properties.Label: Line # Alternate
properties.Description: The Line Alt No contains the Line Number on the Purchase Order or Warehouse Transfer, the Kit Component is tied to. It is not enterable from OE, but is from PO and WT.

properties.Label: Line#
properties.Description: The line number of the order entry line. This field is copied down from the line item the component is on.

properties.Label: Last Change By
properties.Description: Tags the record with the login initials of the last operator to update the record. Last update is defined by the operator pressing GO on a setup screen, or by the completion of a transaction in a batch updating process.

properties.Label: Related Order #
properties.Description: The Order Alt Type contains the Order Number, whether it is a Purchase Order or Warehouse Transfer, that the Kit Component is tied to. This field is not enterable from the OE side, but is from PO or WT.

properties.Label: PO/WT Type
properties.Description: The Order Alt Type contains the Tie type. This denotes whether the Kit Component is tied to a Purchase Order or Warehouse Transfer. This field is not enterable from OE, but is from PO and WT. Content:

properties.Label: Order #
properties.Description: The order number of the component. This field is part of the primary key. Content:

properties.Label: Order Suffix
properties.Description: The order suffix of the component. This field is loaded from the OEEH ordersuf. Content:

properties.Label: Order Type
properties.Description: The order type of a line tie. This field indicates the source for filling the line item (a OE, Bid, WT, or work order). Content:

properties.Label: PD Rec #
properties.Description: The price/discounting record number (from PDSC) used to price this component. If a PDSC record was not found for the component, the pdrecno will be 0. If a PDSC record was used to price the line, the pdrecno is loaded from that PDSC record. This field in conjunction with the company number will allow direct access to the PDSC record. This direct access is used to update the actual quantity on a month/yearly accumulated PDSC record as well as to adjust for special costing (in p-oeeltm.i). Content:

properties.Label: Prev Conv
properties.Description: The previous conversion factor for the component while in change mode. When the line item is accessed in change mode, oeelk.conv is loaded into oeelk.prevconv. When the component is updated, the oeelk.conv may be changed. If so, when GO is pressed on the line item, oeelk.prevconv will be used to back out any ICSW quantities previously updated. This field should be blank except during change mode of the line item. Content:

properties.Label: Prev Product
properties.Description: The previous product for the component while in change mode. When the line item is accessed in change mode, oeelk.shipprod is loaded into oeelk.prevprod. When the component is updated, the oeelk.shipprod may be changed. If so, when GO is pressed on the line item, oeelk.prevprod will be used to back out any ICSW quantities previously updated. This field should be blank except during change mode of the line item. Content:

properties.Label: Prev Qty Ord
properties.Description: The previous quantity ordered for the component while in change mode. When the line item is accessed in change mode, oeelk.qtyord is loaded into oeelk.prevqtyord. When the component is updated, the oeelk.qtyord may be changed. This field should be blank except during change mode of the line item.

properties.Label: Prev Qty Rsvd
properties.Description: The previous quantity reserved is loaded from oeelk.qtyreservd prior to the change to the OE line item. It is used to properly back out the quantity reserved/committed/back ordered when changing the line from entry, during BO fill, during the commit, etc. Content:

properties.Label: Prev Qty
properties.Description: The previous quantity shipped for the component while in change mode. When the line item is accessed in change mode, oeelk.qtyship is loaded into oeelk.prevqtyship. When the component is updated, the oeelk.qtyship may be changed. If so, when GO is pressed on the line item, oeelk.prevqtyship will be used to back out any ICSW quantities previously updated. This field should be zero except during change mode of the line item.

properties.Label: Prev Spec/NS
properties.Description: The previous special/non-stock type is used in change mode on a line item (during entry, BO fill, commit...). It is used to store the oeelk.specnstype prior to allowing change to the line or component. It is necessary to store the old value in order to properly update ICSW (back out then re-add). Content:

properties.Label: Prev Unit
properties.Description: The previous unit for the component while in change mode. When the line item is accessed in change mode, oeelk.unit is loaded into oeelk.prevunit. When the component is updated, the oeelk.unit may be changed. This field should be blank except during change mode of the line item.

properties.Label: Price
properties.Description: The price of the component. This field is stored per special costing unit if the product is specially costed. If not, the price is stored per unit of the component. Content:

properties.Label: Price
properties.Description: The price flag indicates if the price of this component is used in a price roll up for the kit itself. Content:

properties.Label: Price Type
properties.Description: The price type defines a group of products that are similarly priced. This field is used for PDSC level 2, 5, and 8 pricing. It is also used to group products for PDSS pricing. If the component is a non-stock, the pricetype is for informational purposes only. Content:

properties.Label: Print
properties.Description: The print flag indicates if this component is printed on documents. Content:

properties.Label: Processed
properties.Description: This field is used to control the KPEA update recovery logic. It is initially set to no. All component records that have not been processed in KPEA will be read upon F10 update. If the machine goes down during the update, only those components not yet processed will be read for processing when the procedure is reactivated. It is set to yes once all processing is performed on a component through KPEA. Content:

properties.Label: Category
properties.Description: The product category of the line item. On a stock product, this field defaults from ICSP. On a non-stock product, it defaults from OEAO. It is overrideable on the extended screen and the non-stock screen. G/L posting can be done by product category. Content:

properties.Label: Cost
properties.Description: The product cost of the component. If the product is specially costed, this field is represented in the special costing units. If the product is not specially costed, this field is represented in the selling unit on the component. On a stocked product, the prodcost defaults from the ICSW average, standard, replacement, or last cost plus addons (depending on what is appropriate as defined in ICAO). p-oeetlc.i is the include that sets the cost.

properties.Label: Description
properties.Description: The product description of each non-stock product. This field is enterable on the non-stock screen for a non-stock product. The description for a stocked product is not stored on the line item since it is available in ICSP.

properties.Label: Qty From Receivers
properties.Description: If the icsw.reservety = "a" or "r", the system will attempt to allocate inventory immediately. If there is not sufficient available inventory in stock (icsw.qtyonhand - icsw.qtycommit), then the program will attempt to commit inventory from received inventory (icsw.qtyrcvd). This field represents the quantity committed from the received inventory.

properties.Label: Qty Needed
properties.Description: The quantity needed identifies how many of this component, in the unit of measure defined on the component, are needed to build 1 of the kit.

properties.Label: Ordered
properties.Description: The quantity of the product that was requested by the customer. This field is represented in the component unit of measure. It is a factor of of the oeelk.qtyneeded, oeelk.conv, and stock quantity ordered on the kit itself. Content:

properties.Label: Qty Reserved
properties.Description: The quantity reserved indicates how many stocking units of the component have been reserved on this sequence number. Its value will be somewhere between oeelk.stkqtyord and oeelk.stkqtyship based on the availability of the product. More product can be reserved than what is available for all components to ship. (This field was introduced with TB 11896 - Ability to partially reserve component quantity.) Content:

properties.Label: Qty Ship
properties.Description: The stock quantity shipped indicates how many stocking units will be/were used to build the kit. Content:

properties.Label: Ref
properties.Help: User Defined or Reference # (Start With . or #)
properties.Description: The reference of the kit component. This is a user text that is used to print on documents.

properties.Label: Required Component
properties.Description: The required flag defaults from the kit setup (KPSK). It is used to determine if the component is a neccessary component on the kit. If the component is not necessary, it can be deleted. Content:

properties.Label: Requested Prod
properties.Description: The requested product describes the product the customer originally requested. If a customer part number was entered (and cross referenced to a stocked product), the customer part number will be stored in the reqprod. Likewise, if a substitute or upgrade was done, the reqprod will store the originally requested product. This field is used to properly record usage when subs and upgrades are done. Content:

properties.Label: Return Seq#
properties.Description: The return sequence number is used to tie a return line to a sale line. This field on the return line indicates the component sequence number of the sales line.

properties.Label: Territory
properties.Description: The sales territory is stored in OEEL to assist with the performance of Sales Manager reporting. It defaults straight from the OEEH header and is not overrideable.

properties.Label: Seq#
properties.Description: The sequence number defines the sequence of the component. It is part of the primary key along with the company, order type, order, suffix, and line number.

properties.Label: Extended Type
properties.Description: The serial lot type identifies if a component is a serialized or lot controlled product. Content:

properties.Label: Product #
properties.Description: This is the primary product of the component. It indicates the product that was used to build the kit. If a cross reference product was accessed, it is stored in oeelk.reqprod. Content:

properties.Label: Ship To
properties.Description: The customer ship to is stored in OEELK to assist with the performance of Sales Manager reports. It defaults from the ship to entered on the OE banner and is not overrideable at the line level. Content:

properties.Label: Spec/NS
properties.Description: The special/non-stock type describes the Kit Component disposition. It has nothing to do with the OEEL/BPEL specnstype field. If the kit component is a non-stock product (new with Trend 7.0.000), then the oeelk.specnstype will be "n". If the kit component is a stock product that will be handled as a special order item, then the oeelk.specnstype field will be "s". Otherwise the kit component will be a stock product that will be treated as a regular item, so it will be blank. The oeelk.specnstype will no longer have an "L" in it, if the OE line item is lost business. The oeelk.statustype can be used in this case, since it will contain "c" for cancelled. Content:

properties.Label: Status
properties.Description: The status type identifies the status of the line item. It is used to indicate if the line is still active, has been invoiced, or has been cancelled. Content:

properties.Label: Stk Qty Ord
properties.Description: The stock quantity ordered indicates how many stocking units have been ordered by the customer to be used in the kit. Content:

properties.Label: Ship Qty
properties.Description: The stock quantity shipped indicates how many stocking units will be/were used to build the kit. Content:

properties.Label: Sub Product
properties.Description: The substitute flag defaults from the kti setup (KPSK). It indicates if the product for the component can be exchanged during the build for another product. Content:

properties.Label: HS Code
properties.Description: Harmonized System Tariff Code. The HS system uses a logical nomenclature method to categorize goods into approximately 5,000 commodity groups. Countries often assign customs duties based on the harmonized tariff code of the product. Content:

properties.Label: Type

properties.Label: Units
properties.Description: The unit describes the selling unit of measure. It defaults from the ICSW selling unit and can be changed. Validation of the unit in ICSEU or SASTA will set the conversion factor (oeel.unitconv) for the line item. Content:

properties.Help: Assign as PDER contract # for records created from this Method
properties.Description: Added with MSF-179464/SXWEB-13162. Indicates the contract number to be assigned to PDER records created for the alternate rebates which have been setup in PDSRA. Content:

properties.Label: Description
properties.Help: This Will Display as the Name of the Method
properties.Description: Added with MSF-179464/SXWEB-13162. Indicates the description of the calculation method and will display on records setup in PDSRA. Content:

properties.Label: Method #
properties.Help: Defines the Alternate Rebate Methods Available to Use
properties.Description: Added with MSF-179464/SXWEB-13162. Defines the alternate rebate calculation methods to be setup in PDSRA. Method #1 is reserved for the type defined as the Carrier Curve rebate calculation. Content:

properties.Label: Trans Proc
properties.Description: Added with MSF-179464/SXWEB-13162. The function to last update this record. Content:

properties.Label: Spec Rec Link
properties.Help: Special Price/Cost Record Number for Link to Transactions

properties.Label: Actual Cost
properties.Description: The actual cost is updated by EDI processing. It is the actual cost the vendor is basing the rebate on.

properties.Label: Alternate Rebate Record #
properties.Help: Alternate Rebate Record Number Assigned to the Setup of this Rebate
properties.Description: Added with MSF-179464/SXWEB-13162. From the PDSRA Setup screen. This is the Alternate Rebate Record # assigned to the setup of this rebate. Content:

properties.Label: Company #
properties.Description: Identifies the Company under which the record was created.

properties.Label: Contract #
properties.Description: From the PDSR Setup, this is the contract # assign by the user to the rebate setup. It should represent a number given to them by the vendor.

properties.Label: Currency Type
properties.Description: For foreign rebates, the currency of the rebate. Blank is domestic. Content:

properties.Label: Customer #
properties.Help: If Customer Number is 0, the Rebate will Apply to All Custom
properties.Description: Customer #

properties.Label: Division #
properties.Description: Division #

properties.Label: Ship Type
properties.Description: From the PDSR setup screen. W - All Whse Shipments from the Distributor D - Drop Shipments from the Vendor.

properties.Label: Freeze Rebate Type
properties.Description: This defaults from OEAO "Recalc Rebate Through" (sasc.oefrzrebty). It is enterable from OEET F7-Extend if a rebate has been calculated on that product. If a rebate is frozen at a certain stage it will not recalculate at a later stage. For example, if it is frozen at (O)rder Entry, stage 1, it will not recalculate at (I)nvoice Processing, stage 4.

properties.Label: Spec Rec Link
properties.Help: Special Price/Cost Record Number for Link to Transactions
properties.Description: This field will identify the special price/costing data that is related to this record. This number can be matched up to the ICSS record with the primary unique key k-icss.

properties.Label: Claim #
properties.Help: Rebate Claim # Filed with Vendor, Zero for All This Vendor

properties.Label: Invoice Costed Date
properties.Description: If this is a customer rebate or a vendor rebate based on sales, this date will be plugged with the Invoice Date during OEEPI. If this is a rebate based on purchased, it will be plugged with the Costed Date from APETC.

properties.Label: Journal #
properties.Description: Journal #

properties.Label: Line#
properties.Description: If this is a customer rebate or a vendor rebate based on sales, this will be the oeel.lineno. If this is a vendor rebate based on purchase, this will be the poel.lineno.

properties.Label: PO/OE Net Amt
properties.Help: PO or OE Line Net Amount
properties.Description: For customer rebates or vendor rebates on sale, this is the extended net amount based on quantities shipped. For vendor rebates on purchase, this is the extended net amount based on quantities received.

properties.Label: Net Bill Amount
properties.Description: Added with JIRA SXE-944/SXWEB-24367. If APSV.currencyty = " " then netbillfor amount else netbillfor converted to domestic Content:

properties.Label: Net Bill Flag
properties.Description: Added with JIRA SXE-944/SXWEB-24367. Indicates if the rebate is Net Billed. Content:

properties.Label: Foreign Net Bill Amt
properties.Description: Added with JIRA SXE-944/SXWEB-24367. Amount PO line cost was reduced. (could vary from the original Rebate on the PDER). This is assumed to be in the vendor’s currency which could be different than the domestic currency. Content:

properties.Label: Last Change By
properties.Description: Tags the record with the login initials of the last operator to update the record.

properties.Label: Order #
properties.Description: If this is a customer rebate or a vendor rebate based on sales, this will be the oeeh.orderno. If this is a vendor rebate based on purchase, this will be the poeh.pono.

properties.Label: Order Suffix
properties.Description: If this is a customer rebate or a vendor rebate based on sales, this will be the oeeh.ordersuf. If this is a vendor rebate based on purchase, this will be the poeh.posuf.

properties.Label: Original Rebate Amount
properties.Description: Added with JIRA SXE-944/SXWEB-24367. Original rebate amount before it is changed to zero. Content:

properties.Label: Original Foreign Rebate Amount
properties.Description: Added with JIRA SXE-944/SXWEB-24367. Original foreign rebate amount before it is changed to zero. Content:

properties.Label: Spec Price/Cost Unit
properties.Help: Unit of Measure for Price and Cost

properties.Label: Quantity Shipped
properties.Description: At invoicing, if this is a customer rebate or a vendor rebate based on sales, then if the rebate is on a kit component it will be the oeelk.qtyship, otherwise for a regular line item, it will be the oeel.qtyship. At costing, if this is a vendor rebate based on purchase, this will be the (poelc.qtycost / poelc.unitconv).

properties.Label: Rebate Amount Foreign
properties.Description: After OEEPI or SMROR update, this is the rebate amount originally claimed in the vendors currency. But this amount can be changed during the PDER process to the amount the vendor will allow. This amount is used to create AP transactions for foreign vendors.

properties.Label: Rebate Amount
properties.Description: After OEEPI or SMROR update, this is the rebate amount originally claimed in domestic currency. But this amount can be changed during the PDER process to the amount the vendor will allow.

properties.Label: Rebate For
properties.Help: Vendor on (P)urchase, Vendor on (S)ale, or (C)ustomer Rebate
properties.Description: From the PDSR setup screen. C - Customer Rebate S - Vendor Rebate Based on Sales P - Vendor Rebate Based on Purchase

properties.Label: Rebate Percent
properties.Description: This is set from the PDSR setup screen. If the rebate calc type is Net and the Rebate Down To type is Flat, this is 100. If the rebate calc type is Net and the Rebate Down To type is not Flat, then it is the percent entered on the screen. If the rebate calc type is Margin Guaranteed, then this is the Margin % Guaranteed.

properties.Label: Rebate Calc Type
properties.Description: This is set from the Rebate Calc Type from the PDSR setup screen.

properties.Label: Rebate Unit Cost
properties.Description: If the calculation type for this rebate is Net, then the rebcost is the "Rebate From" cost. If the calculation type for this rebate is Margin Guaranteed, then the rebcost is the "Margin Cost".

properties.Label: Reb To Unit Cost
properties.Description: If the calculation type for this rebate is Net, then the rebcostto is the "Rebate Down To" cost. If the calculation type for this rebate is Margin Guaranteed, then the rebcostto is 0.

properties.Label: Record #
properties.Description: From the PDSR Setup screen. This is the Rebate Record # assigned to the setup of this rebate.

properties.Label: Recon Exchange Rate
properties.Description: For foreign rebates, the exchange rate used during PDER to reconcile the rebate. Content:

properties.Label: Ref
properties.Help: User Defined or Reference # (Start With . or #)

properties.Label: Return
properties.Description: For customer rebates or vendor rebates based on sales, this flag will be set to "yes" if this line is a return. This flag is always no for a vendor rebate based on purchase. Content:

properties.Label: Revaluation Number
properties.Description: The number from the most recent revaluation.

properties.Label: Report Exchange Rate
properties.Description: For foreign rebates, the exchange rate when the rebate is claimed through SMROR. Content:

properties.Label: Reported Rebate Amount
properties.Description: This is the original rebate amount (domestic currency) filed with the vendor through the SMROR processs. After the (p)rinted stage, this value is not changed.

properties.Label: Reported Rebate Foreign
properties.Description: This is the original rebate amount (vendor currency) filed with the vendor through the SMROR processs. After the (p)rinted stage, this value is not changed.

properties.Label: Seq#
properties.Description: If this is a customer rebate or a vendor rebate based on sales, this will be the oeelk.seqno. If this is a vendor rebate based on purchase, this will be the sequence of the costing activity for the po line.

properties.Label: Set #
properties.Description: Set number. This represents a transaction within a journal

properties.Label: Ship To
properties.Description: Ship To Identifier

properties.Label: Salesrep In
properties.Description: If this is a customer rebate or a vendor rebate on sale, this is the oeel.slsrepin. If this is a vendor rebate on purchase, this is blank.

properties.Label: Out
properties.Description: If this is a customer rebate or a vendor rebate on sale, this is the oeel.slsrepout. If this is a vendor rebate on purchase, this is blank.

properties.Label: Update Type
properties.Description: To be used for future enhancements.

properties.Label: Status Type
properties.Description: e - Entered through OEET or POEI i - Invoiced through OEEPI or APETC p - Printed through SMROR (Can be set back to "p" in PDER also) u - Updated through PDER d - Disputed through PDER m - Outstanding Sales Manager Issue (???) r - Reconcilled through PDER F10-Update c - Cancelled (Set in OEEPI if qtyship = 0)

properties.Label: Stock Quantity Shipped
properties.Description: At invoicing, if this is a customer rebate or a vendor rebate based on sales, then if the rebate is on a kit component it will be the oeelk.stkqtyship, otherwise for a regular line item, it will be the oeel.stkqtyship. If this is a vendor rebate based on purchase, this will be the poelc.qtycost.

properties.Label: End Date
properties.Description: The ending date for the application of this record. Not every record needs an ending date. If a PDSV record has no ending date it is considered to be in effect until another PDSV record with a later beginning date is created. A PDSV record with an ending date is used only through that date. The record will not be used after that date, regardless of whether another record exists.

properties.Label: Discount
properties.Help: If "Prices" And "Discounts" Exist, "Discounts" Will be Cleared
properties.Description: Discount in percent. This is the discount that will be applied against the 'vendorcost' field. It should be entered as a percent to be taken off, for example 10% off of cost. This is an array of nine elements. The first element will be used until the first quantity break level is reached. At that point the second level will be used until the second level is reached, etc. These levels are used in all programs that calculate the cost of goods for purchasing. This includes POET, POERR, and POERM. Note that price multipliers and discount levels are mutually exclusive. The quantity break points are applied to find EITHER a price multiplier or a discount, not both. Price multipliers take priority over discounts - the discount column will be cleared if the price multiplier column is used.

properties.Label: Price
properties.Description: Price. This field provides a price for the PO. Note that this is an array of 9, each element representing another quantity break. If no quantity breaks are entered the first element will be used. Otherwise, the first level will be used until the first quantity break is met, then the program will proceed to the second level. Note that all prices are considered to be in stocking or costing unit (special pricing/costing) and that all prices are in the currency for the vendor from which the products are purchased. Note also that this is a hard dollar cost, not a multiplier or a percentage. If no quantity breaks are needed or quantity breaks are to be applied against discount levels, the 'vendorprice' field should be used and this field (ALL ELEMENTS) must be set to '0'.

properties.Label: Product
properties.Description: This is a part of the primary key and is validated against ICSP.PROD.

properties.Label: Qty Break
properties.Help: At This Quantity, The Next Level Price or Discount Will be Used
properties.Description: Quantity Break. The quantity breaks refer to total quantity, weight, or cube based on 'buytype'. Note that the figures are per transaction, not cumulative across transactions. This field is an array of 8 elements to be used against 9 price or discount levels. Note that if the transaction meets a given level, the next level of price or discount is used. Examples: Ordered 20, level 2 Qty Break = 20. Level 3 price or discount used. Ordered 18, level 2 Qty Break = 20. Level 2 price or discount used.

properties.Description: Start Date. This field is required, indicating the first effective date of this record. Start date is an element in the primary key for PDSV. This allows two records for the same product but with different start dates. It is not possible to have two records for the same company, vendor, product, and startdt. It is possible to define records with future and past start dates. Future dated records will not become effective until the start date. Back dated records will become effective immediately unless another record exists with a more recent start date (and other valid information), in which case that become effective only if that more recent record expires, is inactivated, or is deleted.

properties.Description: This field is enterable on the PMEP Box Dimension screen if: 1. The PMEP Ship Via is UPSS - UPS Second Day Air or UPSN - UPS Next Day Air. This is new to Trend in 5.1.000f per the new UPS (feb. 7, 1994) upgrade. It is entered by the operator and used to calculate Dimensional Weight. DW = (Height x Width x Length) / 194. Dimesional Weight will override the actual weight if the cubic inches are greater than on cubic foot (H x W x L >= 1728 inches) and the dimensional weight is greater than the actual weight. Dimensional Weight (H, W, L) are required on all Second Day and Next Day Air shipments in PM. Content:

properties.Label: Dimensional Type
properties.Description: This is the Dimensional Weight type. It was added in 5.1.000f for the new UPS Feb. 7, 1994 upgrade. It is set to 'DW' in PMEP when the dimensional weight overrides the actual PMEP weight. The conditions for dimensional weight and how it's used is defined on field dwheight (pmep). This will inform PM that this shipment is using Dimesional Weight vs. Actual Weight. PMEM will exclude dimensional weight shipments for Hundred Weight packages. Also, if the package is dimensional weigth 'DW' will display on the PMEM (Standard and Ground Saver) manifests, on the PMEP screen, when using dimesional weight, on the inquires PMILO, PMILS and the F6-Detail screen for PMILO and F8-Inquiry in PMEP. Also, drives what each weight in PMEP means: 1. If the dwtype 'DW' then pmep.origweight = actual weight and pmep.actweight = dimensional weight. 2. If the dwtype 'DW' then pmep.origweight = 0 and pmep.actweight = actual weight.

properties.Label: Geo Code
properties.Description: Taxware Sales and Use Tax (SUT) uses the geo code to determine which taxes should be applied if there is more than one taxing jurisdiction within a zip code. Examples of this are when a zip code crosses county lines and each county has a different tax rate or when multiple cities exist in the same zip code and each city has a different tax rate. Each taxing jurisdiction within the zip code is given a unique, two-digit identifier. Taxware uses the city name, state, zip code and geo code to find the correct tax rates. Taxware Enterprise (TWE) uses the geo code as a unique identifier of a taxing jurisdiction and not a supplemental identifier as in SUT. With TWE, all jusrisdictions world-wide have a geo code. Each geo code can include country, state or province, county, city and district taxing jurisdictions. Any taxing jurisdiction except country can be omitted from the definition of a geo code. TWE can apply the correct tax rates based on the geo code alone. Content:

properties.Label: Price
properties.Help: Price in POEL before it was possibly changed
properties.Description: This field indicates the POEL.PRICE if the price in the flat file is different than the POEL.PRICE. The price in the flat file will be converted to Trend special price/cost values based on the values in ICSP before this comparison takes place. The price in the flat file may also be a special price/cost number and this will be converted to eaches based on the ICSEU or SASTT conversion value before the price is then converted to the ICSP special price/cost values. If after the conversions, the price from the flat file is different from the POEL.PRICE, the POEL.PRICE will be written to this field before it is possibly updated with the new price. (It may or may not be updated based on the APSE.UPDTPRICE option to update prices.)

properties.Label: Geo Code
properties.Description: Taxware Sales and Use Tax (SUT) uses the geo code to determine which taxes should be applied if there is more than one taxing jurisdiction within a zip code. Examples of this are when a zip code crosses county lines and each county has a different tax rate or when multiple cities exist in the same zip code and each city has a different tax rate. Each taxing jurisdiction within the zip code is given a unique, two-digit identifier. Taxware uses the city name, state, zip code and geo code to find the correct tax rates. Taxware Enterprise (TWE) uses the geo code as a unique identifier of a taxing jurisdiction and not a supplemental identifier as in SUT. With TWE, all jusrisdictions world-wide have a geo code. Each geo code can include country, state or province, county, city and district taxing jurisdictions. Any taxing jurisdiction except country can be omitted from the definition of a geo code. TWE can apply the correct tax rates based on the geo code alone. Content:

table_description: OE line item creation storage table
label: Order Rep 1 Percent

properties.Label: Order Rep 1 Percent
properties.Description: This field stores an additional order rep percentage that can be assigned to an order. Setups in ARSC will copy to ARSS on a copy and can use the AO logic to copy to ARSS if ARSC is changed (SXE-2803). When an order is created, OEEH defaults from ARSC/ARSS and then OEEL defaults from OEEH. The operator can update the assignments in OEEH/OEEL for individual order/line specifics. Once the data is stored in the OEEH/OEEL records in the database, it will be sent to DataLake and any analysis/calculations (usually for commissions) against these fields will be done in Birst. There are five of these fields that can be used. Note that the field number must match to the ordrep field number, i.e., if ordrep2 is assigned a value and you want a percentage related to that, the percentage must be specified in orderreppct2, the 2 must match on both fields to correlate them. Added with JIRA SXE-3048/SXWEB-38216. Content:

properties.Label: CRM Subject Value
properties.Description: What those values do is determine how Contact and Activity Manager (CAM) should run when you select it from the Window menu on that function. For example, if you look at ARSC in the AO/System/Menu Items, you see it has a value of Customer. If you are in ARSC and you select Contact and Activity Manager from the Window menu, the CAM screen that is displayed brought in the information for the current customer and you see all their activities. Similarly, if you look at ICSP in the AO/System/Menu Items, you see it has a value of Product. If you are in ICSP and you select Contact and Activity Manager from the Window menu, the CAM screen that is displayed brought in the information for the current product and you see all activities associated with that product. properties.Label: Geo Code
properties.Description: Taxware Sales and Use Tax (SUT) uses the geo code to determine which taxes should be applied if there is more than one taxing jurisdiction within a zip code. Examples of this are when a zip code crosses county lines and each county has a different tax rate or when multiple cities exist in the same zip code and each city has a different tax rate. Each taxing jurisdiction within the zip code is given a unique, two-digit identifier. Taxware uses the city name, state, zip code and geo code to find the correct tax rates. Taxware Enterprise (TWE) uses the geo code as a unique identifier of a taxing jurisdiction and not a supplemental identifier as in SUT. With TWE, all jusrisdictions world-wide have a geo code. Each geo code can include country, state or province, county, city and district taxing jurisdictions. Any taxing jurisdiction except country can be omitted from the definition of a geo code. TWE can apply the correct tax rates based on the geo code alone. Content:

properties.Label: Geo Code
properties.Description: Taxware Sales and Use Tax (SUT) uses the geo code to determine which taxes should be applied if there is more than one taxing jurisdiction within a zip code. Examples of this are when a zip code crosses county lines and each county has a different tax rate or when multiple cities exist in the same zip code and each city has a different tax rate. Each taxing jurisdiction within the zip code is given a unique, two-digit identifier. Taxware uses the city name, state, zip code and geo code to find the correct tax rates. Taxware Enterprise (TWE) uses the geo code as a unique identifier of a taxing jurisdiction and not a supplemental identifier as in SUT. With TWE, all jusrisdictions world-wide have a geo code. Each geo code can include country, state or province, county, city and district taxing jurisdictions. Any taxing jurisdiction except country can be omitted from the definition of a geo code. TWE can apply the correct tax rates based on the geo code alone. Content:

label: SO Line#

properties.Label: SO Line#
properties.Description: In 4.1.000 this field was renamed from xxi5. It is loaded with an SO Line # through the SWER Labor Time/Entry screen after the work has been completed. When the time entry transaction is 'billed' through the entry function, it gets assigned (added to existing or creates) to a Labor lne. At that point is when the line number gets loaded. Used to track what labor lines the time entry pieces are attached to so they cannot duplicate bill for time.

label: Status

properties.Label: Status
properties.Description: This field initially loads with an 'n' when the SWELJ records are created for time tracking. Once the Time is 'billed' to a labor line item through the SWER Labor Time/Entry function, then the statustype gets set to 'y'. Basically the values mean not billed or billed. In the SWER function in the t-swelj record that displays the trandactions, there is a third type that is only screen related. 'un'billable means the SWEJ transaction associated with the SWELJ record is set to swej.billfl = no. So the time is not billable. Content:

properties.Description: The tax calculated in the jurisdiction. From AP Costing, this is the amount of tax calculated by Taxware Enterprise based upon the information entered for the AP invoice.

properties.Label: Vendor Tax Amount
properties.Description: The portion of the tax the vendor will pay based upon what the distributor is charged on the AP invoice. From AP Costing, the vendor may or maynot include taxes on the AP invoice sent to the distributor depending upon whether or not the vendor has nexus and is required to collect taxes. If taxes are included on the AP invoice from the vendor, the tax liability resides with the vendor instead of the distributor. The distributor will pay the vendor the taxes and the vendor will be responsible for remitting the taxes to the appropriate jurisdiction.

properties.Label: Geo Code
properties.Description: Taxware Sales and Use Tax (SUT) uses the geo code to determine which taxes should be applied if there is more than one taxing jurisdiction within a zip code. Examples of this are when a zip code crosses county lines and each county has a different tax rate or when multiple cities exist in the same zip code and each city has a different tax rate. Each taxing jurisdiction within the zip code is given a unique, two-digit identifier. Taxware uses the city name, state, zip code and geo code to find the correct tax rates. Taxware Enterprise (TWE) uses the geo code as a unique identifier of a taxing jurisdiction and not a supplemental identifier as in SUT. With TWE, all jusrisdictions world-wide have a geo code. Each geo code can include country, state or province, county, city and district taxing jurisdictions. Any taxing jurisdiction except country can be omitted from the definition of a geo code. TWE can apply the correct tax rates based on the geo code alone. Content:

properties.Label: Approval Type
properties.Help: (Y)es, (N)o or Any Other Character For Hold
properties.Description: The approval type of the Value Add transaction. It defaults as "y" unless the transaction was created from an OE order. In that case, it defaults from the OE header (OEEH). A Value Add transaction can not be picked until the approval type is set to "y". Content:

properties.Label: ARP Line
properties.Description: The ARP product line for the finished product on the value add transaction. This field is only loaded for non-stock products. For a non-stock product, this field is enterable on the non-stock screen. For a stocked product, this field defaults from the ARP product line in ICSW. This field is used at the VA header level to further desribe the non-stock product. Content:

properties.Label: ARP Vendor #
properties.Description: The ARP vendor number is for the finished product on the value add transaction if it is a non-stock product. It is loaded with the vendor entered on the non-stock screen. Content:

properties.Label: ARP Whse
properties.Description: The ARP Whse is used if the finished product on the value add transaction is a non-stock product. If the non-stock is also sourced from a vendor through the ARP Whse, the arpvendno and arpprodline will also be loaded. Content:

properties.Label: Assembly Length
properties.Description: Value Add Fabrication Assembly length

properties.Label: BO Exists
properties.Description: Indicates if a back order was created and currently exists on this suffix. Content:

properties.Label: BO #
properties.Description: The number of the suffix this value add transaction was back ordered on. If the bono is 0, a back order has not been generated for the value add transaction (it may be generated in a later stage). Content:

properties.Label: BO
properties.Description: If this field is yes, the suffix is a back order. If no, it is not a back order. Content:

properties.Label: Cancel
properties.Description: The cancel date can be manually entered by an operator. If entered, it indicates that this order must be picked prior to the cancel date or the value add transaction should be cancelled.

properties.Label: Company #
properties.Description: Identifies the Company under which the record was created.

properties.Label: Created Date
properties.Description: Create date is updated when the order or back order is created. It replaces the enter date which used to get updated on copies, back orders, converts, etc. The enter date will remain equal to the date the original order is created.

properties.Label: Cube
properties.Description: The cubes field is the stocking unit cubes for the finished product on the value add transaction. It is defined with more decimal digits than the standard ICSP cubes field to allow user to customize where the cubes came from. In some cases, the actual unit cubes needs to contain more than our standard 2 decimal digits. Content:

properties.Label: Customer Product#
properties.Description: This is a user defined field on the value add transaction header that can be used to store a customers product#. Content:

properties.Label: Division #
properties.Description: The division for the value add transaction. It is used for division GL postings when the value add transaction is completed and received. Content:

properties.Label: EDI 867 VA Components
properties.Help: If yes, Will Include VA Components in 867 EDI

properties.Label: Entered
properties.Description: The date the value add transaction was entered. When a back order is created, the enter date is reset to the date the back order is created. Content:

properties.Label: Enter Time
properties.Description: The time the value add transaction was entered. When a back order is created, this time is reset to the time the back order is created. Content:

properties.Label: Est. Completion
properties.Description: This is the estimated date. It is calculated by the system by taking the number of days to fabricate and adding it to the system date. The number of days to fabricate is taken from the VASP setup for this finished product, or if no setup is found, the ICSW average lead time days is used.

properties.Label: Estimated Cost
properties.Description: This is a user defined field that can be used to store an estimated cost for the finished product. It can be used later to compare the actual cost (vaeh.prodcost) to the estimated cost. Content:

properties.Label: Extended Cubes
properties.Description: The number of cubic units for the finished product for this value add transaction. Content:

properties.Label: Extended Weight
properties.Description: The number of weight units for the finished product for this value add transaction. Content:

properties.Label: Spec Rec Link
properties.Help: Special Price/Cost Record Number for Link to Transactions
properties.Description: This field will identify the special price/costing data that is related to this record. This number can be matched up to the ICSS record with the primary unique key k-icss.

properties.Label: Receiving Jrnl
properties.Description: The journal used when the finished product on the value add transaction is received. This is an VAET journal. Content:

properties.Label: Word Index
properties.Description: Internal field used for keyword processing Content:

properties.Label: Non Stock
properties.Description: The nonstock type field indicates whether the finished product on the value add transaction is a non-stock product or not. A non-stock product will have the letter "n" in this field. If the finished product is not a non-stock then it is considered a stock product (ICSP and ICSW records must exist) and this field will be blank. Content:

properties.Label: Notes
properties.Description: Indicates if the value add transaction has required or non-required notes. Required notes will display in any entry function. Content:

properties.Label: # Times Chg
properties.Description: The number of times the value add transaction header has been changed. Content:

properties.Label: Open Initials
properties.Description: The operator that is currently working on the value add transaction. this field is used to soft lock the order. When entry or maintenance is performed on an order, the openinit is loaded with the current operator. When the operator closes the order, the openinit is cleared. This prevents 2 operators from working on the same order at the same time. We employ soft locking since we are not in a transaction state the entire time an order is entered due to potential lock table overflow problems and length of record lock problems. Content:

properties.Label: Last Change By
properties.Description: Tags the record with the login initials of the last operator to update the record. Last update is defined by the operator pressing GO on a setup screen, or by the completion of a transaction in a batch updating process.

properties.Label: Placed By
properties.Description: The person at the customer's site that placed the order with your company.

properties.Label: Pending Addons
properties.Description: This is the accumulation of all the addon amounts that are considered in a pending status, versus Work In Process (WIP). The value add transaction totals are reflected in the pending status up until a completion activity is performed. A completion activity will move that portion of the totals from the "pending" fields to the "WIP" fields which reflects General Ledger updating that has occured in the WIP GL Accounts. The total value of the finished product always reflects the totals of both the pending amounts and the WIP amounts. Content:

properties.Label: Pending External Charges
properties.Description: This is the accumulation of all the external processes line items that are considered in a pending status, versus Work In Process (WIP). See the pndaddons field for a description of "pending" versus "WIP". Content:

properties.Label: Pending Internal Charges
properties.Description: This is the accumulation of all the internal and inspection processes line items that are considered in a pending status, versus Work In Process (WIP). See the pndaddons field for a description of "pending" versus "WIP". Content:

properties.Label: Pending Internal Estimated
properties.Description: This is the accumulation of all the internal processes line items that are considered in a pending status, versus Work In Process (WIP) that are also classified as "estimated" (versus actual). The estimated amount will be used as the total of the value add transaction up until the time that the actual amounts are entered. Once the actual amounts are entered, then they will be used in the calculation of the total of the finished product for the value add transaction. See the pndaddons field for a description of "pending" Content:

properties.Label: Pending Inventory Amount
properties.Description: This is the accumulation of all the inventory component sections' line items that are considered in a pending status, versus Work In Process (WIP). See the pndaddons field for aa description of "pending" versus "WIP". Content:

properties.Label: Pending Inventory In
properties.Description: This is the accumulation of all the inventory in sections' line items that are considered in a pending status, versus Work In Process (WIP). The inventory in sections are surplus inventory that is to be returned to stock, which is a reduction (credit) of the total of the finished product for the value add transaction. This amount will always be a negative number. See the pndaddons field for a description of "pending" versus "WIP". Content:

properties.Label: Previous VA Order#
properties.Description: This is a user defined field on the value add transaction header screen that can be used to record the previous value add transaction# for this finished product. It is not initialized by the system, rather it is maintained by the user. Content:

properties.Label: Category
properties.Description: The product category for the finished product on the value add transaction if it's a non-stock product. On a non-stock product, it defaults from ICAO. It is overrideable on the non-stock screen. G/L posting can be done by product category. Content:

properties.Label: Cost
properties.Description: The product cost of the finished product. If the finished product is specially costed, this field is represented in the special costing units. If the product is not speially costed, this field is represented in the selling unit from the value add transaction banner. The product cost is calculated by taking the total of all pending amounts (using either the actual or estimated pending internal amount) plus all the Work In Process (WIP) amounts, and dividing by the qty ordered. Content:

properties.Label: Description
properties.Description: The product description of the finished product if it's a non-stock product. This field is enterable on the non-stock screen for a non-stock product. The description for a stocked product is not stored on the value add transaction since it is available in ICSP.

properties.Label: Promised
properties.Description: The date the value add transaction was promised to the customer. The customer will request the order on the requested ship date. Due to stock out problems, drop ship lead times, etc., the promise date is set as an outside service level check. It defaults from the requested ship date but can be overridden.

properties.Label: Ordered
properties.Description: The quantity of the finished product to be fabricated on the value add transaction. This field is represented in the banner unit of measure. Content:

properties.Label: Qty Ship
properties.Description: The quantity that will be fabricated for the value add transaction. It is always set to be the same as the quantity ordered, up until the time the finished product is received. At that time, the actual qty that was fabricated will be obtained from the user and placed in the qtyship. This is needed to determine if a value add transaction backorder should be created. If a value add transaction backorder is created, then the original suffix will contain the qty ordered and the actual qty shipped (different than qty ordered) and a new suffix will be created contain the difference between the 2 qtys from the original suffix and stored in both the qty ordered and qty shipped of the new suffix. The qty shipped is represented in the banner unit of measure. Content:

properties.Label: Ref
properties.Help: User Defined or Reference # (Start With . or #)
properties.Description: The value add transaction reference. This is a used defined field. Content:

properties.Label: Req Ship
properties.Description: The requested ship date of the value add transaction. This is the date the customer would like you to ship the product. Service level analysis can be obtained relative to meeting this date. It defaults to today's date plus the OEAO additional days plus the ICSD cutoff.

properties.Label: Revision #
properties.Description: This is a user defined field on the value add transaction header screen that can be used to record a blue print revision# of the finished product. Content:

properties.Label: Row Pointer
properties.Description: A unique identifier that can be used to link other records to this particular record. Content:

properties.Label: Set #
properties.Description: The set number relative to the journal posting for the receiving of the finished product. This number is incremented for each value add transaction that is received on the journal. Content:

properties.Label: Product
properties.Description: This is the product# of the finished product for the value add transaction. It defines the product that was fabricated for each value add transaction (stocked or non-stock). Content:

properties.Label: Stg
properties.Description: The stage of the value add transaction. Content:

properties.Label: Status
properties.Description: This field indicates whether the value add transaction is active or not. Once a value add transaction reaches received (stage 5) or later, then it is set to inactive. This field is part of indexes to quickly locate only active value add transactions. Content:

properties.Label: Stk Qty Ord
properties.Description: The stocking quantity that will be fabricated for the value add transaction. The quantity is set based on the quantity ordered and the unit of measure for the finished product on the value add transaction. Content:

properties.Label: Ship Qty
properties.Description: The stocking quantity that will be fabricated for the value add transaction. It is always set to be the same as the stocking quantity ordered, up until the time the finished product is received. See the description of the quantity shipped (qtyship) for additional information. The stocking qty shipped is set based on the quantity shipped (qtyship) and the unit of measure for the finished product. Content:

properties.Label: Taken By
properties.Description: The operator that enters the value add transaction. This defaults to the log on operator initials. Content:

properties.Label: Last Change Date
properties.Description: Records the date when a given record was last changed. Last changed is defined by an operator pressing GO from a setup screen, or the completion of a batch processing transaction.

properties.Label: Trans Proc
properties.Description: The function to last update this record

properties.Label: Last Change Time
properties.Description: This is the time portion of the last date/time a given record was changed. Record changed is defined by either an operator pressing GO from a setup screen, or the completion of a processing transaction (ie. Invoiced OE line) in batch type functions.

properties.Label: Type
properties.Description: The transaction type of the value add transaction. This describes the kind of order it is: VA - Regular value add transaction type (reserves inventory, starts off in stage 1) QU - Quote value add transaction (doesn't reserve inventory, starts off and remains in stage 0 "Entered" for it's entire life until converted). DO - Direct value add transaction type (inventory components may be reserved or not, but finished product is not be received in the distributor's warehouse inventory).

properties.Label: Units
properties.Description: The unit describes the selling unit of measure. Validation of the unit in ICSEU or SASTA will set the unit conversion factor (vaeh.unitconv) for the finished product on the value add transaction. Content:

properties.Label: # Stk Units
properties.Description: The unit conversion factor indicates the number of stocking units in a selling unit. If there are 24 stocking units in a case, the unitconv would be = 24. If we are selling 1/6 of a stocking unit, the unit conv would be .16667. This field is used to set the stkqtyord and stkqtyship in the value add transaction for the finished product. Content:

The value add transaction totals are reflected in the WIP status once a completion activity is performed. A completion activity will move that portion of the totals from the "pending" fields to the "WIP" fields which reflects General Ledger updating that has occured in the WIP GL Accounts. The total value of the finished product always reflects the totals of both the pending amounts and the WIP amounts. Content:

properties.Label: WIP External Charges
properties.Description: This is the accumulation of all the external processes line items that are considered in a Work In Process (WIP) status, versus pending. See the wipaddons field for a description of "pending" versus "WIP". Content:

properties.Label: WIP Internal Charges
properties.Description: This is the accumulation of all the internal and inspection processes line items that are considered in a Work In Process (WIP) status, versus pending. See the wipaddons field for a description of "pending" versus "WIP". Content:

properties.Label: WIP Inventory Amount
properties.Description: This is the accumulation of all the inventory component sections' line items that are considered in a Work In Process (WIP) status, versus pending. See the wipaddons field for aa description of "pending" versus "WIP". Content:

properties.Label: WIP Inventory In
properties.Description: This is the accumulation of all the inventory in sections' line items that are considered in a Work In Process (WIP) status, versus pending. The inventory in sections are surplus inventory that is to be returned to stock, which is a reduction (credit) of the total of the finished product for the value add transaction. This amount will always be a negative number. See the wipaddons field for a description of "pending" versus "WIP". Content:

properties.Label: Force Word Index Rebuild
properties.Description: A logical flag that can be assigned opposite of the current value forcing a rebuild of the word index entry for this record. Content:

properties.Label: Write Off Flag
properties.Description: This flag is used to indicate if the cost of the finished product should be "written off" during the receiving of the finished product. This would normally be used by a distributor using an average cost method of inventory valuation, where they don't want the total cost of this value add transaction to effect the average cost of the finished product. Content:

properties.Label: Addons
properties.Description: Each addon entered for a given value add transaction section will be associated with a predefined addon number. Content:

properties.Label: Completed Flag
properties.Description: This flag indicates if the value add transaction section is completed or not. This flag is part of indexes to allow quicker access to open sections. Content:

properties.Label: Company #
properties.Description: Identifies the Company under which the record was created.

properties.Label: Destination Address
properties.Description: Most value add transaction sections define a process that involves inventory. The destination address field contains the address of where the inventory is to be sent. Content:

properties.Label: Destination City
properties.Description: Most value add transaction sections define a process that involves inventory. The destination city field contains the city value of where the inventory is to be sent. Content:

properties.Label: Destination Name
properties.Description: Most value add transaction sections define a process that involves inventory. The destination name field is the name of the organization where the inventory is to be shipped. Content:

properties.Label: Destination Ship From
properties.Description: Most value add transaction sections define a process that involves inventory. The destination ship from# is related to the destination vendor (destvendno) field in that it defined the vendor and ship from# where the inventory is to be sent. Content:

properties.Label: Destination State
properties.Description: Most value add transaction sections define a process that involves inventory. The destination state field contains the state or province value of where the inventory is to be sent. Content:

properties.Label: Destination Type
properties.Description: Most value add transaction sections define a process that involves inventory. The destination type field is used to specify where the inventory is to be sent after that process. Content:

properties.Label: Destination Vendor #
properties.Description: Most value add transaction sections define a process that involves inventory. The destination vendor# field defines the external service vendor where the inventory is to be sent. Content:

properties.Label: Destination Whse
properties.Description: Most value add transaction sections define a process that involves inventory. The destination warehouse specifies the internal processing warehouse that the inventory should be sent to. Content:

properties.Label: Destination Zip Code
properties.Description: Most value add transaction sections define a process that involves inventory. The destination zip code field contains the zip code value of where the inventory is to be sent. Content:

properties.Label: Due Date
properties.Description: If the value add transaction section is an External or Internal processing section, the due date field defines where the process should be completed. Content:

properties.Label: External Ship From
properties.Description: If the value add transaction section is an External processing section, then the external service vendor is defined in the extrvendno field. An optional ship from# can be specified in the extrshipfmno field.

properties.Label: External Vendor #
properties.Description: If the value add transaction section is an External Processing section, then the external service vendor is specified in the extrvendno field. Content:

properties.Label: Goal Description
properties.Description: Each External and Internal processing section defined the intermediate or finished product that is the result of that section. The goaldesc field is the intermediate/finished description for that section. Content:

properties.Label: Goal Product
properties.Description: Each External and Internal processing section defined the intermediate or finished product that is the result of that section. The goalprod field is the intermediate/finished product# for that section. Content:

properties.Label: Goal Ordered
properties.Description: Each External and Internal processing section defined the intermediate or finished product that is the result of that section. The goalqtyord field is the intermediate/finished qty to be produced for that section. Content:

properties.Label: Goal STK Ordered
properties.Description: Each External and Internal processing section defined the intermediate or finished product that is the result of that section. The goalstkqtyord field is the intermediate/finished stocking qty ordered to be produced for that section. Content:

properties.Label: Goal Units
properties.Description: Each External and Internal processing section defined the intermediate or finished product that is the result of that section. The goalunit field is the intermediate/finished unit of measure to be produced for that section. Content:

properties.Label: # Stk Units
properties.Description: Each External and Internal processing section defined the intermediate or finished product that is the result of that section. The goalunitconv field is the intermediate/finished unit of measure conversion factor to be produced for that section. Content:

properties.Label: Internal Whse
properties.Description: If the value add transaction section is an Internal Processing or Inspection section, then the intrwhse contains the warehouse of the branch to perform this operation. Content:

properties.Label: Jrnl
properties.Description: The journal used when this section on the value add transaction is completed. This is an VAET journal. Content:

properties.Label: Manual Zone Flag
properties.Help: Indicates if zone was entered manually by the shipper

properties.Label: Notes
properties.Description: Indicates if the value add transaction section has required or non-required notes. Required notes will display in any entry function. Content:

properties.Label: Last Change By
properties.Description: Tags the record with the login initials of the last operator to update the record. Last update is defined by the operator pressing GO on a setup screen, or by the completion of a transaction in a batch updating process.

properties.Label: # Pick Tickets Printed
properties.Description: The number of times the pick ticket has been printed for this section (Inventory Component sections only). This field is incremented each time a pick ticket is printed for the value add transaction section.

properties.Label: Picked Date
properties.Description: The date the pick ticket was last printed.

properties.Label: Picked Time
properties.Description: The time the pick ticket was last printed.

properties.Label: Picked Initials
properties.Description: The operator that last printed this pick ticket through VAEPP or the demand print (VAETG). Content:

properties.Label: Package Label
properties.Help: This message is printed on each package label

properties.Label: Reprint Pick Ticket
properties.Description: This flag indicates whether the pick ticket needs to be printed or not. When a value add transaction is initially added, this flag is set to yes to indicate that a pick ticket does need to be printed. Once printed, this flag is flipped to no. If a line is maintained or added, the printpckfl will again be set to yes to allow a reprint of the pick ticket.

properties.Label: On Line Processing Flag
properties.Description: This field indicates of an on line process (VAES, POEI, WTEI, VAEI) has begun for this value add transaction section. This field is part of an index that allows quick access to those VA sections that are being processed in a given function. This is needed to separate the on-line screen activity from the actual database updating (F10-Update). Content:

properties.Label: On Line Processing Initials
properties.Description: This field indicates if an on line process (VAES, POEI, WTEI, VAEI) has begun for this value add transaction section. The processinit field contains the initials of the operator who started the on-line portion of the process, but has not completed the processing (F10-Update). This field works in conjuction with the vaes.processfl field. Content:

properties.Label: On Line Processing Proc
properties.Description: This field indicates if an on line process (VAES, POEI, WTEI, VAEI) has begun for this value add transaction section. The processproc field contains the Trend procedure name that started the on-line portion of the process, but has not completed the processing (F10-Update). This field works in conjuction with the vaes.processfl field. Content:

properties.Label: Promised
properties.Description: The date the value add section was promised to the customer. The customer will request the order on the requested ship date. Due to stock out problems, drop ship lead times, etc., the promise date is set as an outside service level check. It defaults from the requested ship date but can be overridden.

properties.Label: Ref
properties.Help: User Defined or Reference # (Start With . or #)
properties.Description: The value add transaction section reference. This is a used defined field. Content:

properties.Label: Req Ship Date
properties.Description: The requested ship date of the value add section. This is the date the customer would like you to ship the product. Service level analysis can be obtained relative to meeting this date. It defaults to today's date plus the OEAO additional days plus the ICSD cutoff.

properties.Label: Route/Day/Stop
properties.Description: The route/day/stop of the value add transaction section. This is used to sort the pick tickets in a order appropriate for delivery. Content:

properties.Label: Row Pointer
properties.Description: A unique identifier for this record. Content:

properties.Label: Section Code
properties.Description: This is the value add transaction section code. Each transaction section contains a user defined table code, defined in VAST. Content:

properties.Label: Section Type
properties.Description: Value add transaction section type. Each value add transaction section will contain one of the allowable section types (not user defined). Content:

properties.Label: Seq#
properties.Description: Value add transaction section sequence#. Each transaction section for a given transaction is assigned a unique sequence#. The sections are listed in this sequence order. Content:

properties.Label: Set #
properties.Description: The set number relative to the journal posting for this section. This number is incremented for each value add transaction that is received on the journal. Content:

properties.Label: Shipped Date
properties.Description: The date the value add transaction section was shipped. It will be automatically updated from the VAES, PM, or (if blank) when the section is completed. It can be manually entered from the shipping feedback screen.

properties.Label: Instructions
properties.Description: The shipping instructions, for the value add transaction section.

properties.Label: Shipped Time
properties.Description: The time the value add transaction section was shipped. This will be automatically loaded from VAes, PM, or (if the ship date is blank) when the value add transaction section is completed. Content:

properties.Label: Ship
properties.Description: This field describes the ship via. It is table driving in SASTT. It describes how the goods are to be sent (IE: via UPS, house delivery, ...) Content:

properties.Label: Specifications/Instructions
properties.Description: All value add transaction sections can contan specification/instruction information. This is a free-form text area containing 11 lines of 60 characters on the screen, but an unlimited number of lines can be entered. The specdata field contains the data which is the result of a Progress V7 editor widget screen. Content:

properties.Label: Print Flag
properties.Description: This flag is used with the specification/instruction free-form text information (specdata) and indicates how this data should be printed. The specprtfl field is used for all sections other than the "SP" (specification/instruction) section itself. Content:

properties.Label: Specifications Print Type
properties.Description: This flag is used with the specification/instruction free-form text information (specdata) and indicates how this data should be printed. The specprtty field is used for the "SP" (specification/instruction) section itself. Content:

properties.Label: Staging Area
properties.Description: The staging area for the value add transaction section. This is particularly important on those value add transactions that are to be staged in the warehouse prior to shipping. If it is not entered on these orders, all "*" will print in the staging area on the pick ticket. Content:

properties.Label: Stg
properties.Description: The stage of the value add transaction section. Content:

properties.Label: Last Change Date
properties.Description: Records the date when a given record was last changed. Last changed is defined by an operator pressing GO from a setup screen, or the completion of a batch processing transaction.

properties.Label: Trans Proc
properties.Description: The function to last update this record

properties.Label: Last Change Time
properties.Description: This is the time portion of the last date/time a given record was changed. Record changed is defined by either an operator pressing GO from a setup screen, or the completion of a processing transaction (ie. Invoiced OE line) in batch type functions.

properties.Label: User 1
properties.Description: User defined field.

properties.Label: User 2
properties.Description: User defined field.

properties.Description: User defined field.

properties.Description: User defined field.

properties.Description: User defined field.
